title: Aeronautical Engineer (level 2/3) - Subsystems
description:
RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available

CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: Yes

CLEARANCE TYPE: Secret

TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

"Please note that this opportunity is contingent on program funding. Start dates are determined after funding confirmation"

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems is currently seeking a Aeronautical Engineer/Principal Aeronautical Engineer to support our B2 Subsystems team of diverse, qualified individuals. This position can be located in Palmdale, CA

The Level 2 or 3 Aeronautical Engineer (AE) – Vehicle Subsystems & Integration be a key contributor, on multiple aspects of aircraft subsystem development. The successful candidate will perform task assignments in electrical, mechanical and or hydraulic design and development.


Key Responsibilities Include:
Develop electrical wiring designs of a functional system including the selection of aircraft-type conductors and electro-mechanical components such as connectors, relays, switches, circuit breakers, terminal junction systems.
• Support design requirements for electrical power generation, conversion and distribution systems, and circuit protective requirements for aerospace vehicle systems including Electrical Loads Analysis, test procedures, power architectures, reports, analyses, and other vehicle power related deliverables.
• Responsible for all aspects of system/component design and development including trade studies, layouts, architecture definition, system test & verification, and troubleshooting.
• May participate on a subcontractor management team and will act as the technical point of contact with suppliers for hardware development, qualification, and procurement
• System level test planning, execution support, verification, data processing, and troubleshooting
• System level evaluations to verify requirements and ensure airworthiness criteria are met
• Create hydraulic and electrical schematics for functional systems, selecting aircraft type conductors and electromechanical components (connectors, relays, switches, circuit breakers, terminal junction systems).


Basic Qualifications:
• Basic Qualifications for Engineer include a Bachelors in Science, Technology, Engineering or Math (STEM) and a minimum of 2 years of experience in Aerospace structural design OR an MS degree in STEM with 0 years of related experience
• Principal: a Bachelors in Science, Technology, Engineering or Math (STEM) and a minimum of 5 years of experience in Aerospace structural design OR an MS degree in STEM with 3 years of related experience
• Strong analytical skills with a track record of complex problem solving
• Experience in electrical design of air vehicle systems
• Your ability to obtain and/or transfer and maintain the final U.S adjudicated government Secret clearance and any program access(es) required for the position within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the Company.

Preferred Qualifications:
Active U.S Government Secret (or higher) clearance (with a background investigation within the past 6 years or enrolled into Continuous Evaluation).
• Experience with military aircraft subsystem development, with requirements definition, specification development, component analysis, procurement, source selection, integration and test and verification for advance aircraft
• Experience interpreting component detail drawings, specifications, installation drawings, and test procedures

#Growth

Primary Level Salary Range: $91,800.00 - $137,600.00

Secondary Level Salary Range: $114,000.00 - $171,000.00

Job title: Associate Director of Affordability - COE - PAP

About the Job:

At Sanofi, we are dedicated to transforming patient health through chasing the miracle of science.

As a prominent pharmaceutical manufacturer, our commitment extends beyond drug development, ensuring that patients can access and afford our therapies.

The Sanofi Patient Support Services (PSS) team is focused on supporting patients wishing to access Sanofi therapies. This is achieved by offering programs that provide reimbursement and logistics support, financial assistance, and patient education. In addition to the program offerings, the PSS organization is also home to field teams that provide education and support to patients and customers.

Join the team transforming care for people with immune challenges, rare diseases, cancers, and neurological conditions. In Specialty Care, you’ll help deliver breakthrough treatments that bring hope to patients with some of the highest unmet needs.

About the Team:

The Sanofi Patient Support Services (PSS) Affordability Center of Excellence (COE) is a team whose mission is to design and govern modular, flexible and scalable affordability solutions that deliver measurable value for both patients and the enterprise, while evolving with a rapidly changing policy and payer landscape.

Our team operates as strategic partners, program architects, operators, and problem solvers.

We are seeking an Associate Director, PAP Operations, to join our team.

Position Overview:

The Associate Director, PAP Operations, will enable operational excellence and implement best practices to support PAP programs. This program will report to the Director, PAP & Free Goods Programs within the Affordability COE.

This role is responsible for the management and implementation of DUPIXENT PAP strategy and may support day-to-day operational oversight and management of other therapeutic areas as needed. This role ensures that the PAP offering operates effectively and evolves in response to market dynamics, supporting patient access to therapies.

About Sanofi:

We’re an R&D-driven, AI-powered biopharma company committed to improving people’s lives and delivering compelling growth. Our deep understanding of the immune system – and innovative pipeline – enables us to invent medicines and vaccines that treat and protect millions of people around the world. Together, we chase the miracles of science to improve people’s lives.

Main Responsibilities:

Program Management & Operations

• Guide and enhance the management of PAP Program(s), including ensuring all SOPs, business rules, process flows and procedures represent best practices from an enterprise-wide Affordability COE perspective.

• Ensure smooth implementation of PAP services for new product indications.

• Support Medicare annual re-enrollment (AR) planning and workflow with HUB vendor including staffing needs, business rule and process alignment, weekly dashboard reporting.

• Monitor changes to Medicare/Medicaid policies and implement and refine processes and/or business rules that align with current landscape (e.g. Low Income Subsidy (LIS), Medicare Prescription Payment Plan (M3P)).

• Develop inventory management protocol with Free Goods pharmacy, ensuring cycle counts are performed and reconciled against shipments. Develop a product forecast to ensure inventory needed for PAP programs appropriate for current health insurance and access landscape.

• Manage patient case escalations as needed.

• Partner with brand PSS Team(s) and Hub Vendor to streamline CRM update requests.

• Ensure all vendors are complaint with regulatory and AE/PV reporting requirements and the Patient Program Tracker reporting requirements.

Program Enhancements

• Implement Affordability enhancements related to PAP and/or Free Goods programs ensuring project plans, deliverables, budgets, and timelines for the program(s) meet enterprise needs.

• Analyze program reports, dashboards, and trends to make recommendations that continuously improve service delivery and better meets patient needs.

• Partner with brand PSS Team(s) and Hub Vendor team to identify opportunities for improvement through quarterly business reviews

Program Communications

• Collaborate and communicate cross-functionally as needed and appropriate with FRMs, PSS Stakeholders, Brand Stakeholders, Analytics & Reporting, Platform, Digital, Legal, and compliance teams about program updates and changes.

• Work with internal PSS brand team(s) to ensure HUB vendor has appropriate program training resources available to them.

• Determine resources that may be needed for Field Teams related to PAP and Free Goods and develop in partnership with our agency of record as well as internal brand marketing teams and internal stakeholders.

About You:

Basic Qualifications:

• BA/BS degree in required.

• 7+ years of experience in affordability program management, patient support services, case management, hub services, or a related field within the pharmaceutical or healthcare industry.

• Excellent understanding of patient affordability issues, access dynamics, policy and payer landscape in the U.S. healthcare system, and best practices in manufacturer free goods programs.

• Ability to travel up to 25% of time.

Preferred Qualifications:

• Ability to create compelling narratives via PowerPoint presentations.

• Be a leader for change.

• Advanced degree (MBA, MFin) preferred.

• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain strong relationships with vendors and internal stakeholders.

• Experience working in cross-functional roles and collaborating with leadership teams.

• Excellent problem-solving skills and analytical with the ability to identify trends and implement improvements.

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to adapt to change in a high-energy and fast-paced environment.

• Ability to influence without authority, including presenting a business case / proposal for change to senior management.

• Ability to provide clear guidance to analytics and reporting teams to enable simple, yet effective and insightful, free goods dashboards.

Why Choose Us?

  • Make your work count by supporting a company that brings life-changing treatments to millions — and is committed to doing right by patients, communities, and the planet.

  • Drive progress from within by helping simplify, scale, and modernize how a global biopharma business delivers smarter, faster, and more sustainably.

  • Support teams across science, medicine, and operations by building better systems, shaping bold strategies, and enabling innovation at speed.

title: Financial Data Analyst

As a Financial Data Analyst, you’ll bring your technical, analytical, and operational support expertise to work alongside thought leaders in data analytics, digital engineering, and financial management on projects supporting operations across EUCOM and AFRICOM Areas of Responsibility. You’ll use your skills and expertise to integrate, analyze, and improve financial data processes and systems that enable mission execution.

Work with us to identify inefficiencies, improve fiscal data workflows, and deliver actionable insights that enhance decision-making, continuity, and operational effectiveness across complex defense financial systems.

This position supports an essential financial data environment and is structured to encompass two skill sets under one role. These include process and change management and program support, driving process improvement, supporting continuity, developing SOPs, helping stabilize and mature financial workflows and reporting, data engineering, and technical analytics supporting data integration, transformation, and analysis across structured and unstructured financial data sources and enabling scalable analytics and reporting. To be successful in this role, you should be comfortable operating in a collaborative environment.

What You’ll Work On:

  • Lead or support change management efforts and workflow improvements.

  • Support continuity of operations by maintaining institutional knowledge, SOPs, and process documentation.

  • Support data validation, quality checks, and compliance-focused financial analysis.

  • Collaborate with stakeholders to improve reporting processes and data usability.

  • Support data transformation, automation, and visualization efforts.

  • Integrate and analyze financial data from multiple systems to ensure accuracy and completeness.

  • Compile, review, and format fiscal data extracts and reports for leadership awareness.

  • Identify trends, recurring issues, and process inefficiencies within financial data workflows.

Join us. The world can’t wait.

You Have:

  • Experience with data exploration, data cleaning, data analysis, data visualization, or data mining

  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data sources

  • Knowledge of financial data workflows, reporting processes, or fiscal data management

  • Ability to communicate analytical findings clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders

title: Campus Director - Warehouse
description:
Roadtex Transportation has become a leader in the nationwide LTL industry, specializing in transporting time and temperature-sensitive products. We handle refrigerated and LTL needs by leveraging no sailing schedules, our nationwide network of 32 strategically placed temperature-controlled facilities, our state-of-the-art tracking, and our specialized equipment and warehousing capabilities. In 2022, Roadtex was acquired by Echo Global Logistics. The acquisition brings a truckload brokerage and expanded transportation management solutions to Roadtex's customers while providing Echo with our national warehouse footprint and advanced temperature-controlled transportation solutions.

Position Summary

The Campus Director is the senior operating leader for the Greenfield Distribution Campus and is responsible for the performance for multi-client within four distribution facilities totaling approximately 2.4 million square feet of ambient and temperature-controlled warehouse space.

This role provides leadership across safety, quality, service, inventory integrity, financial performance, labor, facilities, continuous improvement, and talent. The Campus Director translates client commitments and business requirements into coordinated operating plans while establishing consistent management routines, developing leaders, and removing barriers to reliable execution.

The position serves as a key integrator across Operations, Client Experience, Finance, Human Resources, Safety, Quality, Information Technology, Maintenance, Continuous Improvement, and other enterprise functions.

---

Key Responsibilities

Campus Leadership & Operational Execution

· Lead operating performance across all Greenfield campus facilities and establish clear priorities and accountability.

· Translate business objectives, forecasts, and client requirements into coordinated operating plans.

· Establish consistent daily, weekly, and monthly operating routines to review performance and drive corrective action.

· Identify and resolve cross-site constraints affecting service, productivity, capacity, or cost.

· Partner with support functions within Greenfield and remote locations to accomplish operational goals and expectations

Safety, Quality & Compliance

· Champion a culture in which employee safety, product protection, food safety, housekeeping, security, and procedural discipline are non-negotiable.

· Ensure facilities operate in accordance with company standards, customer requirements, and applicable regulatory requirements.

· Ensure appropriate staffing, training, equipment, and resources are available to support food safety and quality programs.

· Drive timely root cause analysis and corrective action when performance or compliance gaps occur.

Client Service & Business Growth

· Serve as the senior operational partner for clients supported by the campus.

· Ensure reliable execution against service commitments and proactively address emerging client risks.

· Partner with Client Success and commercial teams to support client retention, growth, renewals, and new business opportunities.

· Promote value creation through operational improvement and strong client relationships.

Financial, Labor & Capacity Performance

· Own campus profit-and-loss performance and achievement of budget commitments.

· Manage labor, overtime, productivity, operating expenses, and controllable costs through fact-based decision-making.

· Align staffing and capacity with forecasted demand while protecting service and operational continuity.

· Optimize space, inventory flow, equipment, and resources across campus facilities.

People Leadership & Development

· Lead, coach, and hold site and operational leaders accountable for performance.

· Establish clear objectives and expectations while developing a strong leadership bench and succession pipeline.

· Partner with Human Resources to improve staffing, retention, training, engagement, and performance management.

· Build a high-accountability culture based on collaboration, consistency, and continuous improvement.

Systems & Assets

· Drive adoption of standard work, structured problem-solving, and proven operating practices across campus facilities.

· Ensure effective use and data integrity of warehouse systems and operational technology.

· Ensure facilities, material handling equipment, and preventive maintenance programs support safe, reliable, and scalable operations.

---

Qualifications

Education & Experience

· Ten or more years of progressive leadership experience in warehousing, distribution, fulfillment, value-added services, or related operations.

· Minimum of five years leading managers with demonstrated multi-site leadership responsibility.

· Demonstrated success in a third-party logistics environment with direct client responsibility.

· Experience in food-grade, temperature-controlled, or GFSI-certified environments preferred.

· Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, Engineering, or related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

· Strong financial acumen including profit-and-loss management, budgeting, forecasting, labor planning, and cost management.

· Strong knowledge of warehouse operations, inventory controls, labor management, and warehouse management systems.

· Demonstrated ability to use operational and financial data to identify issues and drive action.

· Experience leading continuous improvement, standard work, root cause problem-solving, and cross-functional change.

· Strong communication, client-management, and organizational leadership capabilities.

Benefits

For more information about our benefit offerings, please visit our careers page at .

title: Sr Quality Control Technician I
description:
By clicking the “Apply” button, I understand that my employment application process with Takeda will commence and that the information I provide in my application will be processed in line with Takeda’s Privacy Notice and Terms of Use. I further attest that all information I submit in my employment application is true to the best of my knowledge.

Job Description

About the Role:

As a Sr Quality Control Technician I, you will play an important role in supporting Quality Control Microbiology operations that help ensure the safety, quality, and compliance of Takeda's pharmaceutical products. You'll perform a variety of biological, chemical, and physical analyses throughout the manufacturing process, from incoming raw materials through in-process materials and finished products.

In this hands-on role, you'll support environmental monitoring, critical utility sampling and testing, endotoxin and bioburden testing, and microbial identification while utilizing laboratory instrumentation and computerized systems such as LIMS to accurately collect, document, and manage data. You'll work closely with Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Engineering, Maintenance, and other site functions to support production activities and maintain a strong culture of quality and compliance.

Your attention to detail, technical skills, and commitment to data integrity will help ensure that Takeda's products meet rigorous quality standards and ultimately reach patients safely.

How You Will Contribute:

  • Perform environmental monitoring and critical utility sampling and testing to evaluate manufacturing environments and critical utility integrity.

  • Conduct biological, chemical, and physical analyses on raw materials, in-process samples, and final products, including endotoxin, bioburden, and microbial identification testing.

  • Perform laboratory assays requiring accurate analytical techniques and application of fundamental biology and chemistry principles, completing routine and special project/protocol testing accurately and within established timelines.

  • Operate laboratory instrumentation and computerized systems, including LIMS, to collect, record, reconcile, and maintain accurate laboratory data and documentation.

  • Maintain data integrity and ensure laboratory activities comply with applicable SOPs, specifications, FDA, GLP, QSR, and cGMP requirements.

  • Maintain laboratory supplies and inventory necessary to support routine testing and perform document requests, archival, and reconciliation activities as needed.

  • Apply continuous improvement practices, including QLP, 5S, LEAN, Standard Work, housekeeping, and GEMBA walks, to support laboratory efficiency and operational excellence.

  • Troubleshoot routine laboratory and testing issues, identify when established practices or procedures are not being followed, and escalate issues appropriately.

  • Collaborate with Manufacturing, Quality Assurance, Engineering, Maintenance, and other support functions to coordinate testing activities, communicate results, and support site operations.

  • Follow all laboratory and site safety requirements, complete assigned training on time, and support additional business needs and projects as assigned.

What You Bring to Takeda:

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemistry, Biological Science, or another related scientific or technical field required; relevant laboratory work experience preferred.

  • Foundational laboratory skills and knowledge of basic microbiology, chemistry, and statistical methods required.

  • Experience with laboratory testing and analytical techniques, including environmental monitoring, critical utility sampling, endotoxin, bioburden, or microbial identification preferred.

  • Knowledge of laboratory equipment and instrumentation, including autoclaves, incubators, and analytical equipment, with the ability to operate equipment in accordance with established procedures required.

  • Strong technical problem-solving skills and the ability to recognize when established practices, procedures, or expected results are not being followed required.

  • Ability to manage multiple tasks concurrently, prioritize activities, and complete testing and documentation accurately and within established timelines required.

  • Ability to read, understand, and follow detailed written procedures and instructions, including SOPs and laboratory methods required.

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to effectively communicate with supervisors, peers, and cross-functional partners required.

  • Proficiency with mathematical calculations and the ability to work with both metric and U.S. measurement standards required.

  • Basic knowledge of chemical and biological safety procedures and demonstrated commitment to maintaining a safe laboratory environment required.

  • Good computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; experience with LIMS or other laboratory information systems preferred.

  • Demonstrated ability to train or assist in training other team members and contribute effectively to interdepartmental teams preferred.

Important Considerations:

At Takeda, our patients rely on us to deliver safe, high-quality products. As a result, we follow strict quality, safety, and compliance requirements throughout our manufacturing and laboratory operations. In this role, you may:

  • Lift, push, pull, and carry up to approximately 25 lbs.

  • Work in controlled environments requiring special gowning and protective clothing over the head, face, hands, feet, and body; additional hearing protection may be required in loud areas.

  • Perform a combination of sedentary work, standing, and walking throughout the facility.

  • Work around chemicals such as alcohol, acids, buffers, and Celite that may require respiratory protection.

  • Work or be assigned to a different shift to meet business needs, including weekends and swing shifts, and must be willing to work off-shift hours.

  • Work supplemental hours as necessary to complete work commitments.

  • Work in confined areas.

  • Work primarily indoors, including areas with clean room and cool/hot storage conditions.

  • Follow all applicable site and laboratory safety rules, GMP requirements, SOPs, and quality procedures.

  • Speak, read, write, and follow detailed written and oral instructions in English.

  • Complete all required training within established timelines.

More About Us:

At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best-in-class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that inspires and empowers you to grow through life-changing work.

Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to deliver Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world

title: Product Developer (Laminated Dough)
description:
Shaw Bakers is growing! As a national leader in the commercial Premium Artisan Bakery category, we are searching for an experienced Product Developer (laminated dough experience required) to join our dynamic team, bringing their pastry/baking culinary expertise to our innovation group.

The candidate will bring extensive knowledge in bakery product development, with a strong focus on lamination techniques, and a proven track record in creating innovative products from concept to commercialization. They will have experience demonstrating both creativity and rigorous technical expertise with industrial food product development. Experience with cookies, bread, or brioche is a plus.


The role involves a mix of office work, lab/kitchen testing, production facility trials, along with visits to suppliers and customers, requiring a self-starter with strong leadership, communication, and collaboration skills. Bi-lingual skills in Spanish and English are highly valuable but not required.


This role is a full-time, onsite position in South San Francisco and we are open to relocation for an experienced candidate.


What You'll Do

  • Product Development: Lead the end-to-end development of innovative bakery products, from ideation to market launch, ensuring alignment with customer requirements and brand standards.
  • Recipe Development: Create and refine detailed paper recipes, including advanced costing, strategic sourcing of ingredients, and proposed labor assumptions, while optimizing for industrial process capabilities and scalability.
  • Documentation: Document formulas, initial cost of goods, labor assumptions, and production processes, ensuring accurate and up-to-date batch sheets.
  • Industrial Pilots: Design and oversee industrial pilot tests in production facilities, organizing up-front test-runs to anticipate potential issues, advise on formula adjustments or needed investments, and optimize processes for consistent quality at scale.
  • Product Quality: Establish and document quality control measures to ensure product consistency and excellence. Define corrective actions with managers and ensure their implementation across departments. Oversee documentation of any production process changes.
  • Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to enhance processes with a continuous improvement mindset, driving efficiency and quality across development and production stages.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Collaborate with operations, packaging engineers, sales, supply chain, and FSQA (Food Safety and Quality Assurance) teams to drive seamless product execution and process improvements.
  • Equipment Strategy: Partner with the engineering team to evaluate and recommend new equipment to enhance product development and production efficiency.

Who We Are


We are the proud artisans behind San Francisco's beloved bakery brand, La Boulangerie, charting a path towards a nationwide presence in the world of CPG. Established in 1996 by French baker Pascal Rigo, La Boulangerie swiftly earned its place as a household name across California. Our unwavering mission from day one has been to bring a little taste of France, with delicious and nutritious food, to as many people as possible.

Fueled by our Bay Area roots, thriving neighborhood cafes, and historical successes, we embark on an exciting journey into larger-scale CPG and wholesale opportunities. Through our past endeavors with industry giants like Starbucks, to today's strategic partnership with Premium Brands, we're forging ahead with creativity and innovation, ensuring that our artisanal baked goods can be accessible to all.


We manage branded products under La Boulangerie and private label products under Shaw Bakers, powered by one united and mighty team. We are bakers and innovators. We are food lovers dedicated to bringing delicious & nutritious food to as many people as possible, making a range of products from breads, pastries, sandwiches, and snacks.Our goal is to balance continual innovation while maintaining French standards for quality and technique.

Today, our customers can sample decadent viennoiserie, mouthwatering sandwiches, and artisanal breads from one of our San Francisco cafes, or pick up their favorite loaf of Croissant Toast and Ham & Swiss Croissants from several fine retailers across the Bay Area and beyond...and we are just getting started!

title: Project Coordinator
description:
Job Title: Project CoordinatorJob Description

The Project Coordinator supports a Senior Project Manager on IT infrastructure initiatives for construction and renovation projects, such as multi-floor facility upgrades. The role begins with administrative and coordination responsibilities and gradually expands to include deeper involvement in project processes. It is well-suited for candidates with 6 months to 3 years of project coordination or related experience, particularly those from administrative, communications, or IT backgrounds who want to grow in IT infrastructure project coordination.

Responsibilities
  • Support a Senior Project Manager in planning and executing large-scale IT infrastructure projects, including multi-floor upgrades and construction or renovation initiatives.
  • Coordinate and schedule project meetings, including preparing agendas, organizing participants, and ensuring appropriate resources and materials are available.
  • Document meeting notes, decisions, action items, and follow-ups, and distribute them to stakeholders in a timely manner.
  • Manage ordering and procurement processes for equipment and materials, including creating and tracking purchase orders and maintaining accurate records.
  • Maintain and update project documentation, including project plans, schedules, reports, and other project artifacts.
  • Assist with project scheduling and project planning activities, ensuring timelines, milestones, and dependencies are clearly documented and communicated.
  • Coordinate site surveys and on-site activities with various IT teams and stakeholders, ensuring logistics and timing align with project needs.
  • Perform basic cost analysis and support budgeting activities by tracking expenses and understanding cost structures, even if not directly responsible for building full budgets.
  • Act as a liaison between real estate teams and project management, ensuring clear communication and alignment on project requirements and timelines.
  • Prepare and maintain reports using Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office tools to track project status, issues, and progress.
  • Ensure timely communication and follow-up on project deliverables under the guidance and supervision of the Senior Project Manager.
  • Support multiple concurrent projects by prioritizing tasks, managing time effectively, and escalating issues or risks when needed.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of project coordination processes by identifying opportunities to streamline documentation, scheduling, and communication.
Essential Skills
  • 6 months to 3 years (up to 5 years) of experience in project coordination or a similar role, ideally in environments involving IT, construction, or facilities projects.
  • Demonstrated experience performing administrative or coordination tasks such as documentation, running meetings, creating or processing purchase orders, and supporting budgeting activities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Microsoft Excel for reporting, documentation, and tracking project information.
  • Experience scheduling and coordinating meetings, including recurring project meetings and cross-functional sessions.
  • Experience supporting project scheduling and project planning activities, including maintaining project timelines and plans.
  • Ability to prepare and maintain project documentation, including meeting minutes, status reports, and project plans.
  • Experience with procurement processes, including equipment ordering and purchase order management.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple tasks, deadlines, and stakeholders simultaneously.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly document and convey information to diverse stakeholders.
  • Basic understanding of IT infrastructure concepts sufficient to coordinate with technical teams and understand project context.
  • Ability to work effectively in a hybrid environment and travel to project sites across Suffolk County as needed.
  • Ability to act as a liaison between multiple teams, ensuring accurate and timely flow of information.
  • Attention to detail and accuracy in documentation, record-keeping, and cost tracking.
Additional Skills & Qualifications
  • Background in administrative, communications, or IT roles that involved coordination, documentation, or stakeholder support.
  • Experience coordinating large-scale projects or site surveys involving multiple IT teams or departments.
  • Familiarity with project coordination or project management practices, including basic knowledge of project plans and schedules.
  • Experience with cost analysis or supporting budgeting activities, even if not responsible for building full budgets.
  • Exposure to IT infrastructure projects in environments such as healthcare, construction, or facilities management.
  • Ability to learn and adapt quickly to new project processes, tools, and technologies.
  • Comfort working under the guidance of a Senior Project Manager while gradually taking on more responsibility.
  • Interest in developing a longer-term career in project coordination or project management, particularly in IT infrastructure.
Why Work Here?

You will join a large, mission-driven organization where you can build your project coordination skills and gain exposure to a wide variety of IT infrastructure and construction-related initiatives. The role offers meaningful opportunities for growth, including the potential to be retained long-term or to interview for full-time positions as you demonstrate your capabilities. You will work with experienced project leaders who provide guidance and mentorship, helping you deepen your understanding of project management practices. The environment supports professional development and encourages individuals who are eager to take on new challenges and expand their responsibilities over time.

Work Environment

The role operates in a hybrid work model that combines remote work with regular on-site presence at project locations across Suffolk County, including sites as far as South Hampton. You will frequently collaborate with IT teams, real estate stakeholders, and project management professionals in both virtual and in-person settings. Work involves using Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Microsoft Excel, for documentation, reporting, and coordination tasks. Site visits may include active construction or renovation environments, requiring comfort navigating facilities and coordinating on-site activities. Work hours generally align with standard business hours, with flexibility needed to attend key meetings and site visits based on project schedules. Dress expectations may vary by setting, with typical business or business-casual attire for office and meeting environments and appropriate, safe attire for site visits as required by project conditions.

description:

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Expand your horizons, advance your career, and contribute to a secure future for generations. Northrop Grumman's Space Sector invites you to bring your pioneering spirit to our collaborative teams. As a Supply Chain Subcontracts Specialist – Level 3 or Level 4, you'll be a linchpin in missions of paramount importance, defining the art of the possible from day one. This position is located in Chandler, AZ. FT remote hybrid work is available, but ability to work onsite in Chandler is mandatory.

Responsibilities:

  • Successful candidate will source and procures specialized goods and services
  • Owns contractual management of the supplier
  • Responsible for source selection from contract proposal to execution phases
  • Coordinates and collaborates with key stakeholders such as contracts, engineering, quality, supplier development, planning, operations, program, and end-users
  • Develops subcontract specifications, work statements, and terms and conditions for the procurement of specialized materials, equipment, and/or services
  • Prepares Request for Proposal package, analyzes and evaluates proposals, negotiates subcontract provisions, selects or recommends subcontractors, writes awards, and administers resulting subcontracts
  • In conjunction with quality organization, evaluates and monitors supplier quality and reliability, as well as supplier ability to support required delivery schedules
  • Identifies strategies and opportunities to reduce cost, improve efficiency and manage risk through strategic and targeted negotiations
  • Manages and leads supplier financial forecasting accuracy

Candidate will also manage performance of subcontracts, ensure compliance with all public law requirements as well as company (and business) policies and procedures including import/export regulations. Employs sound business practices and assesses supplier performance as part of follow-up activities. Ensures that appropriate documentation is provided to logistics/transportation & warehouse organization so that proper receipt is recorded. Manages and develops strategic/key suppliers. Reviews and approves supplier payment as needed. Utilizes process tools such as Lean Six Sigma with suppliers to drive quality, efficiency and continuous improvement.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree and 5+ years of experience in government contracting -OR- Master’s Degree and 3+ years of experience for a level 3
  • Bachelor’s Degree and 8+ years of experience in government contracting -OR- Master’s Degree and 6+ years of government contracting experience for a level 4
  • Experience with FAR provisions and GSC policies and procedures
  • Ability to obtain & maintain a DoD security clearance (US Citizenship Required)
  • Strong knowledge and proven historical performance of cradle to grave subcontract administration
  • Experience preparing subcontractor Request for Proposal (RFP) packages and supporting the NGC acquisition process
  • Experience preparing and presenting briefings to leadership (internal/external)
  • Demonstrated skill and ability to perform professional tasks
  • Strong organizational skills
  • Problem solving aptitude to develop solutions and drive resolution to a variety of problems of moderate scope and complexity
  • Ability to provide accurate supplier invoice and accrual forecasting
  • Ability and willingness to contribute to the completion of organizational projects and goals
  • Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office Applications

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Current & active DoD security clearance
  • Experience managing major subcontracts
  • Experience managing various subcontract types (Firm Fixed Price, Cost Plus Incentive or Fixed Fee, Time & Material, Labor Hour, IDIQ, etc)

title: Civil Project Manager
description:
The Wooten Company’s Winston-Salem, NC office is seeking a team-focused, innovative Civil Project Manager with strong technical experience to join our expanding Civil Team.


Who are you? The ideal candidate is a highly motivated civil engineer with a strong background in successfully completing water, wastewater and / or stormwater projects for both municipal and private clients. You are responsible, work well with a team and communicate well with people of varying backgrounds and experiences. You are eager to learn and grow professionally in your field.


What will you be doing? Candidates can expect to work with utility owners, such as local governments and municipalities, in the delivery of critical water and sewer services, along with other community facilities. The person in this role can make a significant community impact by supporting our clients as they carry out their mission to efficiently own, operate, and maintain public utilities on behalf of their customers / residents. Candidates can expect to be continually challenged to independently design projects that develop solutions to meet our client’s needs, using the right mix of advanced technology and historically successful measures, while working within the financial boundaries of the project stakeholders.


Who will you be working with? The Civil Project Manager can expect cross functional collaboration across all teams and specialties, providing an opportunity to interact with The Wooten Company colleagues in both North and South Carolina. Additionally, this person will regularly work with municipal and private clients, as well as state and federal regulatory agencies. For the right person with a desire to grow professionally, this role is a good opportunity to obtain a depth and breadth of civil engineering ability and to contribute to the growing presence of Wooten, in both the North and South Carolina regions.


Where will you be working? This position is located in our Winston-Salem, NC office affectionately known as the City of Arts and Innovation. Winston-Salem is one of the three cities of the North Carolina Piedmont Triad with Greensboro and High Point completing the trio. title: Automation & Controls Specialist, Infrastructure & Utility (Starship) - Level 4/5
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

AUTOMATION & CONTROLS SPECIALIST (STARSHIP) - LEVEL 4/5

Starship is the largest and most capable space launch system ever developed. With the capability to deliver in excess of 100 metric tons to Earth’s orbit, it will fundamentally change access to space, and is the technology that will be used to establish a self-sustaining city on Mars. We will ultimately need thousands of Starships to accomplish that feat.

The production fluids team is focused on the design and deployment of critical manufacturing and test infrastructure to manufacture & validate vehicle systems prior to flight, enabling high-rate manufacturing. We are looking for enthusiastic and creative individuals to merge rigorous aerospace design with highly reliability industrial fluid systems. As a process specialist, you will be responsible for developing the foundational processes our team requires.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Design, develop, deploy, and manage ground-up automation and controls projects including initial trades, commissioning, hand-off, and training
  • Deep drive process and project specifications for deliverables with design engineers (internal & external) to bound project criteria
  • Design and commission PLC, HMI, and SCADA applications in a high-reliability production environment
  • Design, redline, modify and correct electrical and pneumatic schematics using a mix of in-house and 3rd party tools (Eplan, schematics, etc.)
  • Lay out new industrial electrical control panels which are NFPA79/NEC/UL508A compliant
  • Create and update concise written and visual instructions from design review, technical drawings, and requirement documentation
  • Audit manufacturing process - assessing process inefficiencies, safety improvements, and potential optimizations through the implementation of automation
  • Develop SOW’s, bargain, trade, and release contractor work to enable the in-house build team to keep pace with production needs
  • Proactively utilize JIRA to plan out & complete weekly scheduled tasks

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or equivalency certificate
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience installing, troubleshooting, and maintaining automation and controls systems

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of manufacturing experience in a high-volume production environment
  • 2+ years of experience troubleshooting and programming 6-axis and Cartesian robots
  • Electrical schematic CAD experience using Eplan
  • C#, .NET, python and/or SQL experience
  • PLC programming experience
  • HMI and SCADA programming experience
  • Field bus networks, serial communication and Ethernet communication
  • Hands-on experience building and commissioning high quality electrical control panels and electro-mechanical systems
  • Knowledge of NEC, NFPA 79, UL508A codes
  • Experience in independently troubleshooting advanced electrical circuits, electronic systems, motors & starters, electrically operated equipment and making successful repairs and modifications
  • Proficient in excel, office, and word

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Perform hands-on work in all environments (heat, cold, rain), in tight quarters or at heights
  • Work extended hours and weekends as needed to support launch operations
  • Remain focused in hazardous environments while wearing appropriate PPE
  • Lift up to 50 lbs. unassisted
  • Provide 24/7 on-call support for emergencies

ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

  • To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

  • Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate with all levels of leadership and customers

  • Familiarity with business tools and processes used for scheduling and reporting

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills

title: System Administrator (Top Secret/SCI with Full Scope Poly to start Clearance Required)
description:
North Point Technology is looking to hire a senior System Administrator to support a mission-critical RF and optical capabilities program. This role requires an active Top Secret/SCI clearance with Full Scope Polygraph. The position blends enterprise system administration across Linux and Windows environments with full-cycle network engineering, combining hands-on infrastructure work with automation and security compliance to deliver resilient, high-performance systems for demanding mission workloads.

Responsibilities:

The System Administrator will install, configure, and maintain RHEL/CentOS/Ubuntu/Debian and Windows Server instances while managing users, groups, Active Directory, and local security principals. The incumbent will provision and manage storage solutions including LVM, RAID, SMB, and NFS, and will perform system hardening, patching, and vulnerability remediation against DoD STIG and CIS baselines. Automation responsibilities include developing Ansible playbooks and roles for Linux and Windows workloads, writing Bash, PowerShell, and Python scripts, and operating Ansible Tower/AWX for job scheduling and audit trails. Network engineering duties span the design, implementation, and troubleshooting of enterprise L2/L3 networks including VLANs, routing protocols, QoS, DHCP, and DNS, with specific focus on Arista EOS configuration, CloudVision provisioning, and eAPI/Ansible automation. The role enforces DoD 8570 IAT Level 2 standards, manages secrets and certificates, conducts vulnerability scans, and maintains RBAC across servers and network devices. The administrator will provide Tier 3 support and maintain documentation including designs, runbooks, and SOPs in Confluence or SharePoint with configuration libraries maintained in Git.

Required Skills/Experience:

  • Installation, configuration, and administration of RHEL, CentOS, Ubuntu, and/or Debian Linux servers
  • Administration of Windows Server 2016, 2019, and/or 2022, including Active Directory, user and group management
  • Storage provisioning and management: LVM, RAID, SMB/NFS shares
  • System hardening and vulnerability remediation using DoD STIG and CIS Benchmarks
  • Development of Ansible playbooks and roles for Linux and Windows automation, including use of WinRM modules
  • Scripting in Bash, PowerShell, and Python for task automation and incident response
  • Operation of Ansible Tower or AWX for job scheduling, credential management, and audit trails
  • Git-based version control workflows for infrastructure as code (IaC)
  • Design, implementation, and troubleshooting of enterprise L2/L3 networks: VLANs, BGP, OSPF, DHCP, DNS, QoS
  • Configuration of Arista EOS switches and automation via eAPI and Ansible modules
  • Arista CloudVision for centralized network provisioning
  • High availability network design and capacity planning including EVPN and VXLAN
  • Implementation of network security controls: ACLs, RADIUS/TACACS+, 802.1X, MACsec
  • Role-based access control (RBAC) and secrets/certificate management across servers and network devices
  • Vulnerability scanning and remediation tracking in compliance with DoD requirements
  • Documentation of designs, runbooks, and SOPs in Confluence or SharePoint

Preferred Skills/Experience:

  • Container orchestration using Docker Swarm, Kubernetes, or Apache Mesos
  • Container networking, service discovery, and load balancing
  • Experience with cloud platforms: AWS, Azure, or GCP
  • Use of container registries such as Docker Hub or Google Container Registry
  • Monitoring tools: Nagios, Prometheus, or Grafana
  • Logging tools: ELK Stack, Splunk, or Logstash
  • CI/CD pipeline tools: Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, or CircleCI
  • Pipeline automation, testing, and deployment workflows
  • Networking protocols including TCP/IP and HTTP
  • Storage solutions including SAN, NAS, or Ceph

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in a related discipline, or equivalent experience
  • DoD 8570 IAT Level 2 certification (e.g., CompTIA Security+, CCNA Security, CySA+, or equivalent)
  • Active Top Secret/SCI clearance with Full Scope Polygraph required to start
  • Preferred certifications: RHCE, RHCSA, LFCS, CKAD, or CKA

title: Team Assistant
description:
American Express’s Global Financial Crimes Surveillance Unit (GFCSU) and the US Investigations Unit (USIU), within Global Financial Crimes Compliance (GFCC), in partnership provide end-to-end support and oversight of global financial crimes investigations. In conjunction with GFCC partners, the GFCSU and USIU develop and implement automated transaction monitoring rules, reports, and other processes designed to identify activity potentially indicative of criminal behavior.

The GFCSU and USIU also investigate potentially suspicious financial activity and, when appropriate, file suspicious activity reports (SARs) with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN), which is part of the U.S. Department of the Treasury, and/or refers matters to internal compliance partners for review and reporting globally. In addition, the GFCSU and USIU manage risk associated with politically exposed persons and persons and entities on core sanctions and risk lists through regular screening, and manage risk associated with improper payments that could be indicative of bribery, corruption, or other illicit activity by reviewing internal American Express payments and expenditures.

The GFCSU and USIU together perform a critical role in ensuring that American Express complies with all applicable laws and regulations, including the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), the USA PATRIOT Act, and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, and provides law enforcement with key information for the investigation and prosecution of money laundering and terrorist financing, credit card fraud, identity theft, and other criminal activity.

The successful candidate will work in our hub in Gurgaon (India) to mitigate risk to the American Express enterprise through research and analysis of financial activity for suspicious patterns along with the review of records. Candidates must be flexible and willing to change responsibilities to meet business needs, should be comfortable reading and reviewing records from US jurisdictions, and be able to work with various teams across American Express, including US & International Market Compliance Officers, line of business representatives, and project teams, among others.

  • Conduct investigations across different GFCSU workflows: AML, EDD, Screening and Anti-Corruption.

  • Strong research, report/narration writing, and analytical skills across different GFCSU workflows: AML, EDD, Screening and Anti-Corruption.

  • Reviewing and dispositioning Transaction Monitoring, Screening and EDD alerts,

  • Demonstrate a keen attention to detail in investigation, analysis, and report/narration writing.

  • Meet performance expectations: productivity and quality goals.

  • To develop and maintain an adequate knowledge of the financial crime environment.

  • Excellent verbal and written communications skills
  • At least two years of analytical or investigative experience, preferably within the financial crimes, AML, risk, threat analysis, or fraud fields.
  • Ability to demonstrate an understanding of financial crime typologies and patterns utilized to exploit financial institutions.
  • Ability to synthesize large amounts of information such as transaction data and identify key trends.
  • Ability to work efficiently and independently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Incumbent should be flexible to work in rotational shift environment. Shift window is 24*7 with rotational week offs.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Certification in Compliance, AML or Financial Crime related fields.
  • Experience working in KYC, Transaction monitoring, Sanctions or EDD departments
  • ACAMS or similar certification.

description:

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Join Northrop Grumman on our continued mission to push the boundaries of possible across land, sea, air, space, and cyberspace. Enjoy a culture where your voice is valued and start contributing to our team of passionate professionals providing real-life solutions to our world’s biggest challenges. We take pride in creating purposeful work and allowing our employees to grow and achieve their goals every day by Defining Possible. With our competitive pay and comprehensive benefits, we have the right opportunities to fit your life and launch your career today.

The Naval & Oceanic Systems business unit headquartered in Annapolis, MD is seeking dependable individuals willing to work in a collaborative environment and that are interested in expanding their horizons. The Mechanical Engineering Department is seeking a Staff Materials Engineer with a background in subsea corrosion mitigation.

Essential Functions:

Apply chemistry, physics and materials‑science principles to diagnose material problems and devise solutions, while implementing corrosion‑mitigation strategies for complex systems. He/she researches and evaluates materials and their processing methods to support engineering designs, collaborates with teammates to conduct thorough technical reviews of drawings, specifications and manufacturing plans, and delivers proactive, high‑quality customer service by continually sourcing and sharing relevant information. In addition, the role oversees test activities and test‑article fabrication, documents results, and liaises with senior customer personnel on critical technical issues, often coordinating efforts across organizational boundaries.

The candidate must be able to collaborate in a team environment, lead teams, prioritize and adjust tasks to accomplish the project result, prioritize multiple responsibilities and/or accomplishing them simultaneously, and comprehend and analyze complex problems and develop solutions. Excellent verbal and written communication skills are required.

Basic Qualifications for Staff Materials Engineer:

  • Bachelor’s degree in STEM with 12 years of experience; OR a Master’s Degree in STEM with 10 years of experience; OR a PhD in STEM with 8 years of experience.

  • Basic understanding of the processes that produce corrosion (uniform, galvanic, crevice, etc) and the strategies that mitigate it.

  • Practical understanding of additive manufacturing modalities and alloys.

  • Basic knowledge of metallurgical practices (e.g., weld, metallurgy, metallographic evaluation, heat treatments, fracture mechanics, corrosion control, and failure analysis).

  • Basic knowledge of coating types and coating application methods used to prolong life of marine systems.

  • Basic understanding of principles related to cathodic protection.

  • US Citizen with the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Familiarity with Navy / DoD processes and workflow.

  • Detailed knowledge of coating types and coating application methods used to prolong life of marine systems.

  • Familiarity with the properties of and design considerations pertaining to non-metallic materials such as urethanes, adhesives, and composites.

  • Detailed knowledge of principles related to cathodic protection and ability to specify cathodes of subsea systems.

  • Active Top Secret/SCI clearance.

About the Role

We are seeking an analytical and detail-oriented Inventory Reserves Analyst to support inventory valuation and reserve accounting activities within a global manufacturing environment. This role will be responsible for preparing and analyzing inventory reserve calculations, investigating reserve drivers, supporting month-end close and audit activities, and ensuring compliance with internal controls and accounting policies.

  • Support SOX compliance, audit requests, and maintenance of audit-ready documentation.
  • Develop recurring reports and perform ad hoc analyses to support business decision-making.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to understand inventory risks and reserve drivers.
  • Assist in process improvement and automation initiatives related to inventory reporting and analysis.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field.
  • 2+ years of experience in inventory accounting, cost accounting, financial analysis, or manufacturing finance.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data interpretation skills.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel; experience with SAP, Power BI, Tableau, or similar tools is an advantage.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work across multiple functions.

Preferred Experience

  • Exposure to semiconductor or manufacturing environments.

title: Copilot, Cowork & Copilot Studio Governance Engineer
description:
Description

Our client is rapidly adopting Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Cowork, and Copilot Studio agents, and needs governance to keep pace with that adoption. This contract Copilot Engineer will stand up and operationalize agent governance across the tenant, including agent sharing and exemption controls, inventory and risk baseline, high-exposure remediation, data-protection controls, safe adoption, and knowledge transfer so the program is self-sustaining when the engagement ends.

Engagement objectives

• Agent sharing governance — tenant-wide restriction plus exemption request/approval workflow — operational in the Microsoft 365 Copilot Control System.

• Complete, maintained agent inventory with a transparent, repeatable risk-scoring model.

• Remediation of the highest-exposure agents, including action-taking / connector agents and agents with embedded firm data.

• Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and DLP applied across agents and their grounding data; labeling gaps closed.

• Pay-as-you-go / Copilot Credits monitoring, billing-policy guardrails, maker enablement guardrails, runbooks, and knowledge transfer.

Key responsibilities

• Configure and maintain agent access, sharing, publishing, lifecycle governance, approved-publisher model, and exemption workflow with Information Security.

• Govern Copilot Studio declarative and custom-engine agents; configure Managed Environments, environment routing, connector/DLP policies, and least-privilege controls.

• Build and maintain the tenant agent registry/inventory; risk-score custom actions, data-source scope, embedded files, sharing breadth, and labeling gaps.

• Baseline, prioritize, and remediate high-exposure agents; report progress to IT leadership.

• Align agent controls with the firm's confidentiality and client/matter obligations, including ethical-wall considerations.

• Produce maker guidance, guardrails, standards, runbooks, and documentation; support Desktop Experience and AI Solutions on agent access and adoption.

Required qualifications

• 5+ years of hands-on Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra administration, with recent, demonstrable focus on Copilot and/or Power Platform governance.

• Hands-on experience administering Microsoft 365 Copilot (Copilot Control System) and building and governing agents in Copilot Studio and Agent Builder.

• Power Platform admin center: Managed Environments, DLP / connector policies, and environment strategy.

• Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and data loss prevention; governance experience operationalizing controls and lifecycle processes at scale.

• Automation with PowerShell and Microsoft Graph; excellent documentation, stakeholder communication, and knowledge-transfer skills.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience with Microsoft Copilot Cowork and/or Microsoft Agent 365.

• Familiarity with ethical walls, matter security, pay-as-you-go metering, and Copilot Credits.

• Relevant Microsoft certifications (e.g., AI Administrator Associate, Power Platform, Security/Identity, Information Protection / Purview).

• Prior experience in a law firm, professional services, or another regulated, confidentiality-sensitive environment; familiarity with ethical walls is a plus.

Engagement details

• Duration: 6-month fixed-term contract; full-time (~40 hrs/week); possible extension by mutual agreement.

• Work model: US-remote

• Hours: standard US business hours with overlap to New York (Eastern Time).

• Reports to: Manager, Cloud & Authentication Services.

• Target start date: immediate

  • 11 paid Holidays

As a Patient Service Representative (PSR), you will serve as the first point of contact for patients, providing exceptional customer service and administrative support. In this role, you will help ensure a positive patient experience and support the efficient operation of the clinic by coordinating communication between patients and healthcare staff.

Key responsibilities include welcoming patients and visitors, answering routine inquiries, screening and directing calls, scheduling appointments, maintaining patient records, verifying insurance eligibility and benefits, collecting copays and outstanding patient balances at check-in, and assisting patients with portal enrollment. The PSR is also responsible for performing general clerical and administrative functions that support the daily operations of the primary care clinic.


Responsibilities:


Medical receptionist

  • Greet and welcome all patients: Creating a friendly and welcoming environment is paramount, setting the tone for the entire patient visit. This involves greeting patients and visitors in person and over the phone professionally.
  • Announces patients, visitors as needed with sensitivity.
  • Interact with fellow workers in a way that promotes a respectful and cooperative working environment
  • Assists nurses, physicians, and other clinical and/or medical staff l with administrative support
  • Accurately and efficiently respond to tasks received from providers, other office staff, and billing
  • Open and close the patient waiting room
  • Utilize spare time in work related activities which contribute to the clinic's needs
  • Must adhere to policies, procedures and regulations as outlined in the office policy and procedures manual

Registration and Information Management

  • Register patients using EMR.
  • Coordinates and prepares patient’s appointments and itinerary
  • Check insurance eligibility and verification on every patient
  • Collect and scan insurance and other required documents
  • Check report to ensure coverage and proper co-pay collection
  • Confirm insurance eligibility and verification prior to scheduling new patient appointments
  • New patient intake including entry into EMR
  • Verify and update patient demographic and insurance details at each visit.
  • Collect identification and insurance cards, copying or scanning them for the patient's record.
  • Scan other relevant patient information into the Electronic Medical Record (EMR).
  • Enters data from source documents into computer following format displayed on screen and enters necessary codes; compiles, sorts and verifies accuracy of data to be entered; responds to inquiries regarding entered data and makes corrections as necessary
  • Retrieves patient records, test results and/or charts from outside sources
  • Prepares paperwork and patient records related to their area of responsibility

Financial Responsibilities

  • Collect co-pays and past due balances on patient accounts. Process payments and issue receipts. Handle insurance inquiries and verify insurance eligibility.

Appointment Management

  • Optimize provider schedules by efficiently scheduling and confirming appointments. Answer phones, taking messages, and making appointments.
  • Calling and rescheduling cancellations.
  • Monitor’s voicemails and returns calls
  • Creates reminder calls

Patient Support and Communication

  • Answer patient inquiries, provide general information, and address concerns. Help patients complete medical forms and guiding them on next steps. Ensure patient privacy and confidentiality, following HIPAA regulations.
  • Invites every patient to join the patient portal and includes proper paperwork and education to the patient
  • Patient check-out.
  • Act as a liaison between patients and healthcare providers.
  • Maintain and update patient records. Maintain office inventory and equipment, including ordering supplies. Maintain cleanliness and organization of the reception area.
  • Creates and mails patient letters (no show and 3 call attempt)
  • Provides assistance to patients and family members; refers questions to the appropriate department or individual
  • Maintains, sorts, files, and obtains patient records, files and/or charts

  • Backup for Medical Records
  • Assists in training other staff members on the appropriate use of equipment, office systems and work procedures as requested
  • Assists other departments with administrative duties, as requested
  • Prepares other written documentation as required by the profession and the department; maintains, distributes, analyzes and projects information for required records, reports and statistics, as directed
  • Update HealtheLink, as requested
  • Performs other related duties as assigned or requested

description:
Description

description:

Job Description

Senior Director, Global Commercial Transformation

About the Role

The Senior Director, Global Commercial Transformation is responsible for leading the coordination and execution of global commercial transformation programs that advance Takeda’s commercial priorities and enable business growth. This role identifies strategic opportunities and internal/external issues that may impact commercial effectiveness, and translates strategic direction into coordinated action across global and regional stakeholders.

The role ensures clear alignment on deliverables, interdependencies, commercial capability requirements, risks, and execution plans. As a senior leader, this position plays a critical role in driving enterprise-wide collaboration, supporting decision-making, and enabling successful delivery of transformation initiatives over the short- to mid-term horizon.

How You Will Contribute

  • Lead the coordination and governance of global commercial transformation programs across multiple workstreams, ensuring delivery against defined objectives, milestones, and outcomes.
  • Partner with global, regional, and functional leaders to establish priorities, clarify accountability, and align on program scope, dependencies, and timelines.
  • Identify and manage key risks, issues, and interdependencies that could impact delivery, escalating appropriately and enabling timely resolution.
  • Define and prioritize commercial capability requirements required to support transformation objectives and future operating model needs.
  • Develop and maintain program roadmaps, governance structures, reporting mechanisms, and leadership updates to ensure transparency and execution discipline.
  • Facilitate cross-functional collaboration across commercial, strategy, operations, digital, and enabling functions to support integrated execution.
  • Synthesize complex information, key decisions, and progress updates into concise, executive-ready communications for senior leadership.
  • Support change management, business readiness, and adoption planning to help ensure transformation initiatives are effectively implemented and sustained.
  • Influence across a matrixed global organization and lead through multiple layers of management without direct authority where required.
  • Contribute to the development of short- to mid-term plans for optimizing commercial organization capabilities and transformation priorities.

Skills and Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience leading global commercial transformation, strategic program management, business planning, or related enterprise initiatives.
  • Strong capability in coordinating complex, cross-functional programs in a global, matrixed organization.
  • Proven ability to drive accountability for deliverables, timelines, dependencies, and decision-making.
  • Experience identifying commercial capability gaps and translating business needs into actionable transformation plans.
  • Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills, including the ability to partner effectively with senior leaders.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and risk management skills.
  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with executive audiences.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience across multiple layers of management and diverse geographies.
  • Strong understanding of commercial operating models, transformation governance, and enterprise change execution.
  • Experience in a global biopharmaceutical or similarly complex, regulated environment preferred.

Leadership Expectations

As a leader of a major country, multiple smaller countries, or a regional/global functional area, your accountability extends to shaping operational strategy, integrating activities within Takeda, and possibly contributing to broader business strategy. You may also be responsible for leadership through at least two levels of subordinates and for influencing outcomes across the enterprise.

Education and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
  • 10 - 15 years of experience in commercial strategy, transformation, operations, or program leadership required; experience in Pharmaceutical industry preferred.
  • Experience working in a global, matrixed organization strongly preferred.
  • Strong understanding of commercial pharmaceutical business and operations.
  • Previous people leader experience preferred.

More about us:

At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best in class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that will inspire and empower you to grow through life-changing work.

Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace, in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to deliver Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world.

This position is currently classified as "hybrid" in accordance with Takeda's Hybrid and Remote Work policy.
