-Ensure seamless integration of capabilities, epics, and features with ground satellite software systems solutions

-Utilize Atlassian tool suite, including Jira dashboards and Confluence knowledge bases

-Support and/or lead preparation and execution of milestones and Agile product increments

-Engage with multiple working groups and control boards

-Additional specifics of responsibilities can be tailored based on the skillset and experience of the selected candidate

Basic Qualifications for Systems Engineer – Level 3:

-Bachelor's degree in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) discipline with 5+ years of engineering experience OR

-Master's degree in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) discipline with 3 years of experience OR

-PhD degree in STEM discipline with 1 year of experience

-Candidate must have an active SCI at time of application and prior to start date. Continued employment thereafter will be subject to maintenance at the level of clearance and program access required for the position in the future.

-Experience with developing and evaluating behavioral and structural architecture diagrams using MBSE (Model Based Systems Engineering) methodology and tooling or equivalent

-Experience using No Magic Cameo or equivalent

-Experience with space-vehicle, command-and-control, mission management, mission data processing, or software subsystems

-Demonstrated written and oral communications skills through written requirements, test, and evaluation criteria

-Experience with Systems Engineering processes and artifacts development in support of SW development, including use cases, interface control documents, class diagrams, sequence diagrams, database design, schema development, and SW protocols such as REST, HTTP, & RESP or equivalent

-Experience working on Agile programs and methodology

-Experience working with Space Vehicle Subsystems including thermal, power, attitude control system, propulsion, and/or communications

title: Senior Product Manager, Internal Agentic Processes
description:
• Change the game for how work gets done at Zip, turning agentic AI opportunities into practical products that make a meaningful difference for our teams
  • Bring strong product discovery and product management experience, plus a practical understanding of AI, automation and agentic technologies
  • Work flexibly from our Sydney or Melbourne office, partnering closely with Data & AI and teams across Zip

Write your story with a career at Zip

As Senior Product Manager, Internal Agentic Processes, you’ll help shape how Zip uses agentic AI to create smarter, simpler and more effective ways of working.

Working closely with our Data & AI team and teams across the business, you’ll uncover the internal processes where agentic capabilities, including Zed, Zip’s internal AI capability, can create the greatest value.

You’ll own the product problem, use case, workflow and outcome, taking opportunities from discovery and prioritisation through experimentation, implementation and adoption. Data & AI will be your key technical partner, bringing the underlying AI and engineering capability to life.

This is an opportunity to help Zip build a practical understanding of what agentic AI can unlock, redesigning how work gets done rather than simply automating the way it happens today.

What you’ll own

  • Identify and prioritise internal processes and workflows where agentic AI can improve effectiveness, efficiency and quality
  • Lead product discovery with internal teams to understand their workflows, pain points, needs and opportunities
  • Build and manage a prioritised pipeline of agentic AI opportunities, balancing business value, user impact, feasibility, risk and strategic alignment
  • Define clear product outcomes, requirements and measures of success, using sound judgement to navigate ambiguity and make considered trade offs
  • Partner closely with Data & AI to turn business problems and workflow opportunities into practical, scalable solutions
  • Lead experiments and pilots that test assumptions and determine where agentic approaches should be adopted, adapted or stopped
  • Redesign internal workflows around new capabilities, looking beyond automation to find better ways for teams to work
  • Drive adoption by ensuring successful solutions are intuitive, useful and embedded into everyday workflows
  • Use data, feedback and operational insights to understand impact and continuously improve delivered solutions
  • Capture reusable product patterns and learnings that help successful agentic use cases scale across Zip
  • Partner with Risk, Security and other stakeholders to ensure responsible AI practices and appropriate controls are embedded from the outset

What you’ll bring to the team

  • Zipsters work on a broad range of initiatives, and our skills and experiences all look a little different. What really matters to us is that you’re a great fit with our four Values, and have a desire to learn and grow.
  • So whether you meet some or all of the desirable attributes below, we’d still love to hear from you:
  • Strong product management experience, with the ability to take complex opportunities from an ambiguous problem through discovery, delivery and continuous improvement
  • Strong product discovery skills and an ability to understand complex workflows, uncover underlying problems and translate them into clear product opportunities
  • A practical understanding of AI, automation and agentic technologies, with the judgement to recognise where they can create meaningful business value
  • Experience partnering with Data, AI, Engineering or other technical teams to turn business problems into scalable product solutions
  • Strong systems and process thinking, with an ability to connect the dots across people, processes, data and technology
  • Experience using experimentation, data and qualitative insights to prioritise opportunities and make effective product decisions
  • Strong communication and stakeholder influencing skills, with the ability to navigate competing priorities and bring people with you through change
  • Commercial and operational judgement, balancing business value, user experience, scalability, delivery complexity and risk
  • A mindset that embraces AI and new tools to adapt, learn and grow.
  • An aptitude for identifying and managing risks. Whether you are a People Manager or an Individual Contributor, we are all leaders at Zip, therefore effective risk management is important to how we run our business and part of all our roles.
  • Our values in your DNA. Customer First, Own It, Stronger Together and Change the Game.

What you’ll get in return

As we write this next exciting chapter in our story, we will continue to move at pace and embrace change. For you, this might mean opportunities to learn new skills with hands-on experience, broader responsibilities, or the buzz of seeing your work impact customers faster.

Zip is a place where you’ll get out exactly what you put in. When you join the team, we'll do our best to make sure you can be yourself and surround yourself with smart, friendly colleagues and leaders who have your back, so that you can make the big things happen.

Zipsters tell us these are just some of the best things about working here. You’ll also receive:

  • 25 days paid leave annually, including birthday leave and quarterly wellbeing days
  • 16 weeks paid parental leave for primary carers, and 4 weeks for supporting carers
  • Family support policies including miscarriage bereavement leave and domestic violence leave
  • Mental health and wellness initiatives, including $299 annual wellbeing allowance, free access for you and family members to our EAP service Sonder, discounted private health insurance and great rates on fitness sessions through ClassPass
  • 2 days paid volunteering leave per year
  • Access to the Flare Benefits Hub and Novated Leasing for savings across lifestyle, essentials and wellbeing
  • Fee-free Zip products, and discounts with Zip merchant partners (AU)
  • Team social events, epic offices, free breakfast daily, and weekly free lunches (Sydney and Melbourne)

Be a part of a team that reflects the diversity of our customers

We pride ourselves on being a workplace that provides equal opportunities to people of all ages, cultural backgrounds, sexual orientations, gender identities, abilities, veteran status, and everything else that makes you unique.

Equally, we’re committed to ensuring our recruitment processes are accessible and inclusive. Please let us know If there are any adjustments that need to be made to ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.

And finally…get to know us

Zip Co Limited (ASX: ZIP) is a digital financial services company, offering innovative, people-centred products that bring customers and merchants together.

Operating in two core markets - Australia and New Zealand (ANZ) and the US, Zip offers point-of-sale credit and digital payment services, connecting millions of customers with its global network of tens of thousands of merchants.

We’re proud to be a values-led business and our values - Customer First, Own it, Stronger Together and Change the Game - guide us in everything we do.

We are seeking Customer Complaint Resolution Specialists to join a large financial services organization supporting escalated customer concerns through a dedicated Single Point of Contact (SPOC) team.

As a member of the Single Point of Contact (SPOC) team, you will serve as the primary liaison for customers who have active complaint cases. Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Defense Systems is seeking a Principal Electrical/ Sr. Principal Electrical Engineer Technical Lead for the team. This position is located in Roy, UT and supports the Sentinel program.

What You’ll Get To Do:

This candidate will join the Sentinel Launch Systems Infrastructure Facility Electrical Design (FED) Team. This role will serve as a system and/or equipment design engineer on the Facility Electrical Design Team. Candidates must be able to understand the intent of Weapon System design at a general level and follow direction on how that informs facility power system design and equipment design decisions. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong work ethic, and must possess fundamental electrical engineering skills. Demonstrated ability to foster diverse and inclusive teams with high levels of engagement, including receiving mentoring and coaching from leads is required. Excellent verbal and written communication skills are required, and the ideal candidate will have demonstrated success in collaborating with Engineering teams and associated stakeholders.

Roles & Responsibilities:

  • Supporting design requirements for electrical power generation, conversion and distribution systems, and circuit protective requirements for ground systems including Electrical System Analysis, test procedures, power architectures, reports, analyses, and other power related deliverables.

  • Attending internal program, customer and/or supplier technical exchange meetings and/or formal program milestone reviews to provide and/or obtain progress status updates.

  • Working in a fast-paced work environment with high expectations, significantly diverse assignments, and collaborative/team settings across all levels.

  • Ensure appropriate coordination between facility electrical design and other integration teams.

  • Integration and documentation of electrical systems designs for the weapon system. Coordinate electrical system engineering content and work products.

  • May perform research, evaluation, and systems integration in electrical or electro-mechanical systems, cables, connectors, power systems, test equipment, and more.

  • Possess strong interpersonal skills to work effectively to understand system level interdependencies that impact electrical requirements and design constraints.

  • Demonstrate leadership principles – Integrity, respect, organizational, communication etc.


Basic Qualifications:
Principal Engineer Electrical:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) discipline from an accredited university and 5 years of experience, or 2 years of experience with a Master’s degree, or 1 years of experience with a PhD.

Sr. Principal Engineer Electrical:

  • Bachelor’s degree in a Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) discipline from an accredited university and 9 years of experience, or 7 years of experience with a Master’s degree, or 4 years of experience with a PhD.

Both Levels:

  • Must be a US Citizen with an active DoD Secret Clearance.

  • Must have the ability to obtain and maintain Special Access Program (SAP) approval within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs.

  • Knowledgeable with Siemens Teamcenter PLM or equivalent.

  • Electrical engineering experience in at least two of the following fields: electrical architecture, power system and power equipment design, development and test of mixed signal circuits, interface definition (internal and/or external), or power distribution.

  • Experience utilizing power-system design and/or analysis software tools such as ETAP, PSS/E, SKM?(PTW), Easy?Power, PSCAD or equivalent.

  • Knowledge of industry/military codes and standards, including mil-specs, IEEE, NEC, NESC, NFPA, IEC, and UFC.

  • Experience with creating and executing to schedule & technical recovery plans.

  • Ability to meet program technical, cost and schedule milestones.

  • Working knowledge of Microsoft (MS) Office Suite (Word, Excel, Power Point

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Working experience designing, troubleshooting (RCA) and/or implementing ground power systems, facility power systems and/or launch power systems.

  • Revit experience.

  • Experience with high-power and/or high-frequency systems, including power electronics.

  • Knowledge of EMI/EMC design, shielding techniques, and thermal management for electronic systems.

  • Authorship and release of engineering documentation including technical drawings, specifications, and test procedures.

  • Familiarity with DoD acquisition processes, milestone reviews, and government contracting.

  • Experience maintaining and reporting status of program activities

description:
ABOUT GREYSTAR


Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. Headquartered in Charleston, South Carolina, Greystar manages and operates over $350 billion of real estate in more than 260 markets globally with offices throughout North America, Europe, South America, and the Asia-Pacific region. Greystar is the largest operator of apartments in the United States, managing over one million units/beds globally. Across its platforms, Greystar has nearly $79 billion of assets under management, including over $34 billion of development assets and over $36.5 billion of regulatory assets under management. Greystar was founded by Bob Faith in 1993 to become a provider of world-class service in the rental residential real estate business. To learn more, visit .

JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY

This position performs technical and mechanical work that ensures the physical aspects of the buildings, grounds, amenities, and common areas of the property meet the Company’s standards for cleanliness, appearance, safety, and overall functionality.

Property Type: Stabilized

Unit Count: 1228
Schedule: Monday-Friday; 9am-6pm *subject to change depending on business needs.

Essential Responsibilities:
1. Completes assigned work orders generated from resident requests for service, as well as preventative maintenance on the property by diagnosing the source or cause of the defect or problem, and making repairs in accordance with established policies, procedures, safety standards, and code requirements.

2. Completes the “make-ready” process to prepare vacant apartment homes for leasing and new move-ins by completing the pre-move-out inspection, creating a “punch” list of maintenance work needed, scheduling vendors and contractors as needed, obtaining needed supplies and materials, completing all maintenance tasks, and inspecting completed work.

3. Follows procedures for accessing and obtaining materials, supplies, equipment, tools, and other items from the property’s maintenance department by tracking inventory used, returning unused items to the established location, and notifying the maintenance supervisor about re-ordering needs.

4. Completes documentation and other paperwork in a timely, accurate, and complete fashion so that service requests can be appropriately documented and tracked.

5. Assists in maintaining the grounds, common areas, and amenities by picking up trash and debris, pressure-washing breezeways and pool areas, performing general cleaning, and painting curbs and signage as needed.

6. Supports cost-cutting and expense control programs by fixing rather than replacing parts when possible, not being wasteful with materials and supplies, and practicing the correct use for tools and equipment.

1. Complies with Greystar’s safety and risk-management policies by attending and participating in the property’s routine safety meetings, completing required training on OSHA and other safety related laws and requirements, and by reporting accidents and incidents promptly and accurately.

Service Technician

In this role, you will play a key part in supporting the end-to-end recruiting process, including resume management, interview scheduling and logistics, meeting and room coordination, candidate travel arrangements as needed, expense processing, and offer preparation.

As an integral member of the recruiting team, you will serve as a primary point of contact for candidates and help deliver a seamless, professional, and positive experience for both candidates and hiring managers. You will work closely with recruiters, candidates, interviewers, and business leaders across multiple cities, countries, and time zones, ensuring clear communication and effective coordination throughout the recruiting process.

The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. This role requires sound judgment, discretion, professionalism, and the ability to remain composed and responsive under pressure.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate a high volume of interviews and related logistics, including video conferences, office visits, phone screens, and debrief meetings.

  • Provide timely, professional, and responsive communication to candidates throughout the recruiting process.

  • Support recruiters with the preparation and distribution of offer letters and the collection of new-hire documentation.

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with candidates, recruiters, interviewers, and other key stakeholders.

  • Manage a high volume of candidate activity, scheduling requests, and competing priorities.

  • Coordinate candidate travel and expenses, as needed.

  • Support additional recruiting initiatives, projects, and administrative responsibilities as assigned.

Experience Required

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.

  • 1–3 years of experience supporting a recruiting or talent acquisition team, or 1–3 years of experience as an Executive Assistant in a high-volume, fast-paced environment.

  • Experience within management consulting, financial services, or another professional services environment is preferred.

Technical Skills

  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office.

  • Experience with applicant tracking systems is preferred.

  • Working knowledge of recruiting policies, procedures, and applicable employment practices is a plus.

Skills and Attributes

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to independently prioritize and manage multiple responsibilities.

  • Strong calendar management and scheduling skills.

  • Ability to effectively manage both individual and shared team inboxes.

  • Demonstrated ability to thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

  • Strong judgment and discretion when handling confidential and sensitive information.

  • Excellent interpersonal and relationship-building skills.

  • Strong customer service orientation and a commitment to delivering a positive candidate experience.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to manage multiple projects and adapt quickly to shifting priorities and deadlines.

  • Fluency in English.


Oliver Wyman is a business of Marsh (NYSE: MRSH), a global leader in risk, reinsurance and capital, people and investments, and management consulting, advising clients in 130 countries. With annual revenue of over $27 billion and more than 95,000 colleagues, Marsh helps build the confidence to thrive through the power of perspective. For more information, visit oliverwyman.com, or follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Marsh is committed to creating a diverse, inclusive and flexible work environment. title: Director of Compliance and Risk (UK)
description:
About BJAK

BJAK is Southeast Asia’s largest digital insurance platform, expanding financial access through automation, data, and digital scale. As we grow across markets, we are committed to building a platform that is safe, compliant, and trusted.

We are hiring a Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) to lead regulatory strategy, risk governance, and compliance operations for our UK market entry and expansion alongside the CEO. This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA.

This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function.

Why This Role Matters

The Director of Compliance and Risk (UK) will:

  • Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services.

  • Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements.

  • Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices.

  • Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders.

  • Build compliance capability and culture across the company.

What You Will Do

Regulatory Leadership & Strategy

  • Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements.

  • Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision.

  • Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies.

  • Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly.

Risk Governance & Compliance Operations

  • Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance.

  • Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps.

  • Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance.

  • Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised.

Consumer Protection & Business Integrity

  • Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation.

  • Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight.

  • Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards.

Cross-Functional Support & Training

  • Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution.

  • Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models.

  • Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities.

You Will Thrive in This Role If You

  • See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker.

  • Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail.

  • Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic.

  • Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments.

  • Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation.

What You Bring

  • 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech.

  • Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements.

  • Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred).

  • Proven ability to design policies, conduct risk assessments, and manage complex compliance programs.

  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, including dealing with regulators.

Bonus (Nice to Have)

  • Experience in start-up or high-growth environments.

  • Previous SMF experience.

  • Background in insurtech, digital distribution, or online marketplaces.

  • Knowledge of GDPR, AML, sanctions, or cross-border compliance.

Location Requirement

  • This role is based in the UK. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our London office at least 3 days per week.

Why Join Us

  • Shape compliance for a fast-growing international fintech-insurtech platform.

  • Build frameworks that enable safe, inclusive financial access at scale.

  • Work closely with leadership and regulators to drive responsible innovation.

  • Competitive compensation with long-term growth and international career opportunities.

Compensations Range

  • We offer a highly competitive package, ranging from £100,000 to £150,000, reflecting both experience and suitability for this pivotal role.

title: Professional Land Surveyor - Wilmington, NC
description:
The Wooten Company’s Wilmington, NC office is seeking a Professional Land Surveyor who will work closely with the Geomatics Practice team. This position provides the opportunity to be an essential part of the growth of our Geomatics practice while also being an integral participant in the continued growth of our firm.


Who are you? The Professional Land Surveyor will be comfortable in managing numerous and varying projects simultaneously and bring self-motivation, initiative, and energy to the Geomatics Department. You will be able to take survey data and make it walk and talk, understanding the importance of the legal aspects of surveying, and working through potential problems. You will know when to ask questions and when to forge ahead independently.


What will you be doing? The Professional Land Surveyor will be responsible for addressing the project needs of internal and external clients by providing high quality and efficient service with professional integrity and exemplifying the corporate vision and core values of The Wooten Company. These responsibilities include but are not limited to: preparation of scope and fee proposals; consideration of applicable resources, tools, and methods; survey calculations for existing conditions and existing and proposed property and easement lines; and production and certification of plats for topographic, property, and easement surveys. These responsibilities also include interpretation of construction plans and using best practices for calculating horizontal and vertical location of construction stakes.


Who will you be working with? The Professional Land Surveyor will be working directly with external and internal clients and survey field and office technicians for a variety of land surveying projects.


Where will you be working? Our Wilmington office is located in the heart of downtown Wilmington on the corner of Front St. and Grace St. With a view of the river and the famous Cape Fear river walk just a couple blocks away, there are many restaurants and beautiful places to frequent either on your lunch break or after a day at the office. Parking downtown is also free to employees! Besides the quaint downtown river scene, you will be minutes away from Wrightsville, Carolina, and Kure beaches, as well as Fort Fisher State Park and aquarium, and plenty of shopping and foodie destinations.

The Practice Architect II (PA II) position is a leadership position in the organization that is responsible for managing multiple consulting and delivery projects and account teams/programs. The PA II provides consulting and delivery assurance of services for clients through a range of internal and external functions in the following areas: Consulting, Account Interaction, Service Delivery and Practice Delivery responsibilities.

The position of Practice Architect II is distinguished from more senior Practice Architect positions by the nature of the engagements or programs involved; deal sizes range from transactional solutions of < $1M to multi year outsourcing solutions of > $20M. As a second level Practice Architect, a PA II is expected to have the experience and background to perform all the duties described below for engagements that are focused on consulting/delivery management within the defined subject matter area, including resource management, deliverables development, project planning and executions, adherence to contract attributes and costing, customer interaction, and other key aspects of solution based managed services.

For a PA II, these engagements will typically be delivered for a North America customer or at the customer location, usually North American based. They are expected to have adequate level skills required for complex deliverable-based, fully outsourced, or extremely large scale engagements or programs and lead the delivery effort to a larger cross-functional project/program. • Capture, develop, and refine intellectual property (IP) based upon projects, programs, and engagements; develop IP to be reusable for future training and delivery requirements.

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. The selected candidate will design and develop multimedia learning solutions for an Army Air Defense System that includes defense against manned aircraft; rockets, artillery, and mortars; unmanned aerial systems (UAS); and cruise missile defense.

This requisition may be filled at the Multimedia Designer or Principal Multimedia Designer level:

  • Principal Multimedia Designer - Bachelor's degree in Instructional Systems Design, Instructional Technology, Human Performance, Training and Learning Development, Psychology, Marketing, or related discipline (and 5 years of relevant experience); or 3 Years with Masters; 0 Years with PhD) or 9 years of experience in lieu of degree may be considered

  • Design, develop, write and edit technical documents such as technical procedure manuals, user manuals, training materials to communicate clear and effective instructions to a wide range of audiences to include military personnel.

  • Experience working in ADDIE and other training development models for technical disciplines
  • Knowledge of human performance processes to breakdown knowledge and skill gaps to identify appropriate learning solutions
  • Multimedia design experience (audio/video editing, 2D/3D design, animation, software simulation, etc.)
  • Experience executing and delivering training system products on large DoD military program

title: Information Management Specialist
description:
Job summary

Across government, the effective management of information is fundamental to transparency, accountability and good decision-making. As organisations generate increasing volumes of data and content, the ability to manage information throughout its lifecycleensuring it is secure, accessible and complianthas become a critical capability. At Ofgem, strong information management underpins regulatory effectiveness, supports legal obligations and ensures that information can be trusted and used to deliver better outcomes.

Ofgem plays a vital role in protecting energy consumers and supporting the UKs transition to a more secure, fair and sustainable energy system. As the organisation continues to evolve, maintaining high standards of information and records management is essential to ensuring compliance with legislation, safeguarding information assets and enabling effective collaboration. Working within the newly formed Data, AI & Information Governance team, in Digital Data & AI, this role contributes directly to ensuring Ofgem meets its statutory and regulatory responsibilities.

As an Information Management Specialist, you will play a key role in strengthening Ofgems information and records management framework. You will support the development and maintenance of policies, processes and standards that underpin information governance, while providing practical advice and guidance to colleagues across the organisation on information handling, records management and lifecycle requirements.

This is a role with meaningful organisational impact, combining policy, governance and hands-on delivery. You will work across teams to embed best practice, support compliance with legislation such as the Freedom of Information Act and Data Protection Act, and help ensure that information is well-managed and used appropriately in line with government standards.

Job description

You will be responsible for:

  • Providing expert advice and guidance on information and records management, helping colleagues apply best practice and meet organisational and regulatory requirements.
  • Supporting the development and maintenance of Ofgems information management policies, processes, and guidance to ensure they remain effective and up to date.
  • Developing and maintaining retention and disposal schedules for electronic and physical records, throughout their lifecycle.
  • Working with teams across the organisation to promote good information management practices and support compliance with corporate policies and relevant legislation.
  • Delivering training, guidance and awareness activities to build capability and improve understanding of information and records management responsibilities.
  • Conducting information audits and reviews to ensure information assets are appropriately managed, safeguarded, and subject to the correct controls.
  • Collaborating with Information Assurance, Digital and Technology colleagues to identify management risks and support appropriate mitigation activities.
  • Supporting the procurement, implementation and ongoing management of information systems and services, ensuring implementation management requirements are considered throughout.

We are looking for an experienced information and records management professional with a strong understanding of information governance and lifecycle management within a large or complex organisation. You will have practical experience applying information management policies and processes, alongside a good understanding of relevant legislation, including the Freedom of Information Act and Data Protection legislation.

You will be confident providing advice and guidance to colleagues, supporting teams to meet information management requirements and promoting good practice across the organisation.

Experience within government, the public sector or a regulated environment would be beneficial, particularly where information is managed in line with UK Government standards and guidance. Knowledge of Machinery of Government processes and records management best practice would also be advantageous.

This is an opportunity to play an important role in ensuring Ofgems information is managed effectively, securely and compliantly. Working with colleagues across the organisation, you will help support good practices and ensure Ofgem meets its statutory and regulatory obligations.

Person specification

Essential Criteria

  • Proven experience in an information and records management role, with responsibility for managing information throughout its lifecycle, including review, retention, disposal, transfer and preservation of records (Lead Criteria).
  • Can demonstrate a working knowledge and application of relevant Information and Records Management legislation and codes of practice (Lead Criteria).
  • Can demonstrate experience of developing, implementing, maintaining or improving information and records management policies, processes, standards or governance frameworks.
  • Proven experience of providing advice, guidance, training or support to colleagues and stakeholders to improve compliance with information and records management requirements.
  • Can demonstrate experience of monitoring, assessing or assuring compliance with information and records management requirements, including an understanding of Machinery of Government processes and their impact on the management, transfer, ownership, retention and disposal of information and records.

Desirable Criteria

  • Can demonstrate knowledge of the UK government standards for Information and Records Management and experience applying these in a public sector environment.

#LI-DNI

Behaviours

We'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:

  • Making Effective Decisions
  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Delivering at Pace

Benefits

Alongside your salary of 35,232, OFGEM contributes 10,206 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme. Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).

Ofgem can offer you a comprehensive and competitive benefits package which includes; 30 days annual leave after 2 years; Excellent training and development opportunities; The opportunity to join the generous Civil Service pension which also includes a valuable range of benefits; hybrid working (currently 1 day a week in the office but this is kept under review), flexible working hours and family friendly policies. Plus lots of other benefits including clean and bright offices based centrally, engaged networks and teams and an opportunity to contribute to our ambitious and important targets of establishing a Net Zero energy system by 2050. This exciting blend of professional challenge and personal reward identifies career opportunities at Ofgem as something to get excited about.

Things you need to know

Artificial intelligence
Artificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.

Selection process details

This vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window) , and will assess your Behaviours and Experience.

When you press the Apply now button, you will be asked to complete personal details (not seen by the sift panel), your career history and qualifications.

You will then be asked to provide a 1250 word personal statement evidencing how you meet the essential and desirable skills and capabilities listed in the role profile. Please ensure you demonstrate clearly, within your supporting statement, how you meet each of the criteria listed in the role profile. In the event of receiving a large number of applications, an initial sift may take place on just the lead criteria indicated in the essential criteria.

The personal information we have collected from you will be shared with Cifas who will use it to prevent fraud, other unlawful or dishonest conduct, malpractice, and other seriously improper conduct. If any of these are detected, you could be refused certain services or employment. Your personal information will also be used to verify your identity. Further details of how your information will be used by us and Cifas, and your data protection rights, can be found by [ https://www.cifas.org.uk/fpn ].

At Ofgem, we expect our staff to carry out their roles with honesty, fairness and openness. They should follow the Civil Service code and be free from any influence or bias. We are committed to making sure interests are recognised, declared and managed appropriately so that we can fulfil our duties as an energy regulator. Our Conflicts of Interest policy outlines the types of interests Ofgem staff must declare before onboarding, and the rules they must follow throughout employment so that we can clearly demonstrate that our decisions are not influenced by private interests.

Security

title: Full-Time Store Merchandising Supervisor (Rehire/Referral)
description:
Role Specific Information

Job Description

About the Role

As Merchandising Supervisor you will be the expert in merchandising and leading associates to deliver excellent customer service through sales floor merchandising, pricing and recovery. You will teach, coach, develop and supervise associates while consistently executing merchandising processes.

What You’ll Do

  • Execute store merchandising standards following visual merchandising direction, accomplishing product presentation; make decisions about and adaptations to merchandising direction based on the layout, adjacencies and needs of the store in partnership with the Merchandising Manager

  • Maintain a well recovered selling floor where product is displayed in a manner that is clear, easy to understand and compelling to the customer

  • Maintain appropriate levels of product on the sales floor by remerchandising and replenishing as necessary based on sell through and seasonal changes

  • Coach, teach and train merchandising associates to accurately and efficiently execute company merchandising direction to brand standards

  • Execute pricing activities in store, ensuring that price changes, sign changes and ticketing procedures are completed accurately and efficiently

  • Support the training of associates on merchandising standards, product knowledge, and tools adhering to Kohl’s brand standards

  • Support and partner with the Operations team on merchandising incoming product, ensuring efficient execution

All Supervisor roles at Kohl’s are responsible for:

  • Leading with integrity, honesty and fostering teamwork in an engaged and inclusive culture

  • Exercising good judgment; taking appropriate partners as needed

  • Modeling, guiding and providing direction to associates

  • Demonstrating and coaching a customer service mindset, including customer service philosophies, anticipating customer needs and satisfactorily resolving issues

  • Leading by example by personally meeting or exceeding individual goals (e.g., productivity, credit, loyalty)

  • Supporting strong operational standards, shortage mitigation, and merchandising presentation to include accurate pricing and proper signing

  • Preventing loss by educating associates, monitoring daily store activity, maintaining product protection standards, ensuring company policies are followed and partnering with Loss Prevention

  • Monitoring and adjusting resources as dictated by the business to support customer needs and workload demands when assigned as leader on duty

  • Use key performance indicators (KPIs) to make informed business decisions that drive overall store results

  • Accomplishing multiple tasks within established timeframes

  • Training, monitoring and reinforcing company policies, procedures, standards and guidelines

  • Maintaining adherence to company safety policies for the safety of all associates and customers

  • Key holder responsibilities include opening and closing store processes, and providing direction to associates

  • Other responsibilities as assigned

​

What Skills You Have

Required

  • Must be at least 18 years of age or older

  • Strong verbal/written communication and interpersonal skills

  • Flexible availability, including days, nights, weekends, and holidays

Preferred

  • 2 years experience in retail or similar industry

  • Experience supervising teams or associates, including the responsibility for coaching to achieve daily performance goals

Essential Functions

The requirements listed below are representative of functions you will be required to perform, however you may be required to perform additional functions. Kohl’s may revise this job description at any time. To perform this job successfully, you must be able to perform each essential function satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions, absent undue hardship.

  • Ability to perform the accountabilities listed in the “What You’ll Do” Section.

  • Ability to satisfactorily complete company training programs.

  • Ability to comply with dress code requirements.

  • Basic math and reading skills, legible handwriting, and basic computer operation.

  • Ability to operate and communicate on multiple frequency devices, handheld scanners, and other technology equipment as directed.

  • Ability to maintain prompt and regular attendance and meet scheduling requirements as set by the company.

  • Perform work in accordance with the Physical Requirements section.

​

Physical Requirements

  • Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. frequently and occasionally over 50 lbs. with a two person lift.

  • Ability to climb, squat, stoop, kneel, crouch, bend, twist, reach, lift, grasp, push and pull on a frequent basis.

  • Ability to stand/walk for the duration of a scheduled shift (at least 8 hours).

  • Ability to visually verify information and locate and inspect merchandise.

  • Ability to comply with health and safety standards.


Pay Range: $23.50 - $36.45

title: Epic Credentialed Trainer
description:
Epic Credentialed Trainer

100% On-Site

Augusta, Georgia

Project Overview

We are seeking experienced Epic Credentialed Trainers to support a large healthcare system as newly acquired locations transition onto the Epic platform. The role will play a critical role in preparing end users for a successful system adoption by delivering workflow-based training and providing hands-on support throughout the implementation process.

As an Epic Credentialed Trainer, you will work directly with physicians, nurses, office staff, and other clinical and operational users to ensure they are confident using Epic workflows. Following training, you will provide At-The-Elbow (ATE) support during go-live activities, helping users navigate the system in a live patient care environment.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced Epic Credentialed Trainer who thrives in fast-paced healthcare environments and enjoys supporting organizations through large-scale Epic transitions.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver instructor-led Epic training sessions to clinical and non-clinical end users.
  • Facilitate workflow-based education for newly acquired home health and hospice locations.
  • Serve as an Epic Credentialed Trainer by providing expert guidance on Epic functionality and best practices.
  • Provide hands-on At-The-Elbow (ATE) support during and after go-live activities.
  • Assist end users with workflow adoption, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.
  • Partner closely with operational and project teams to ensure a seamless Epic transition.
  • Support one or more of the following Epic applications:
    • Ambulatory Cadence
    • Ambulatory Dorothy Comfort
    • Dorothy Comfort Home Health & Hospice
  • Reinforce learning and promote user confidence throughout the implementation process.

Qualifications

  • Active Epic Credentialed Trainer status in one or more of the following applications:
    • Ambulatory Cadence
    • Ambulatory Dorothy Comfort
    • Dorothy Comfort Home Health & Hospice
  • 3 to 5+ years of recent Epic training experience.
  • Proven experience delivering instructor-led Epic training programs.
  • Prior At-The-Elbow (ATE) support experience during Epic implementations or go-lives.
  • Strong communication, presentation, and end-user support skills.
  • Experience supporting Epic implementations, acquisitions, upgrades, or optimization initiatives is highly preferred.
  • Ability to quickly build rapport with clinical and operational staff while serving as an effective Epic Credentialed Trainer.

Additional Project Details

  • Initial engagement is approximately 6 weeks.
  • Position requires onsite support.
  • Some trainers may be required to conduct Saturday training sessions.
  • Project kickoff is scheduled for September.
  • Trainers will support end users across multiple newly acquired healthcare locations.

Why Join This Opportunity?

This Epic Credentialed Trainer opportunity offers the chance to make an immediate impact on a major healthcare system transformation. These individuals will work alongside experienced implementation teams, support end-user success, and contribute directly to a smooth Epic adoption across home health and hospice environments.

﻿Apply Today

If you are an experienced Epic Credentialed Trainer with a passion for end-user education, workflow optimization, and go-live support, we encourage you to apply and become part of this exciting Epic implementation initiative.

title: Director of Deployment, Field Communication
description:
Job Description

Director of Deployment, Field Communication

Department

Customer Operations / Field Delivery

Reports To

Chief of Staff (dotted line to CEO on deployment escalations)

Location

Remote (U.S.) — see Travel Expectations

FLSA Status

Exempt

Role Summary

The Director of Deployment, Field Communication owns the end-to-end post-sale deployment lifecycle for Mutualink’s Field Communication products across our public safety, federal, and critical infrastructure customer base. This is a customer-facing delivery leadership role that translates closed-won opportunities into operational outcomes — on-time, on-spec deployments, accelerated time-to-value, and deployment-quality customer relationships that fuel renewal and expansion.

The role sits at the intersection of Customer Operations, Sales, and Customer Success. The Director is the single accountable owner for Field Communication deployment delivery from contract handoff through customer acceptance, and partners with the VP of Growth on pre-close deployment scoping for fleet and federal opportunities. Performance is measured on deployment delivery KPIs and on the expansion Annual Contract Value (ACV) that high-quality deployments produce.

Scope of Responsibility

Deployment Delivery

  • Lead end-to-end deployment of Field Communication solutions for SLED, federal, and enterprise customers, from contract handoff through customer acceptance.

  • Build and continuously refine repeatable deployment playbooks across single-site, multi-site fleet, and tactical / Go-Kit form factors.

  • Own deployment delivery Service Level Agreements: on-time / on-spec completion, customer sign-off, time-to-first-value, and time-to-full-adoption.

  • Serve as the single accountable owner for deployment escalations spanning Engineering, Sales, and Customer Success.

Customer-Facing Leadership

  • Act as the senior Mutualink point of contact for the customer through deployment, including agency leadership, IT, and operational stakeholders.

  • Run kickoff, status, milestone, and acceptance meetings with public-safety and federal customers.

  • Manage field training and customer enablement to ensure users are operationally proficient at go-live.

  • Drive deployment-quality customer health that supports renewal, multi-year conversion, and ACV expansion.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner with the VP of Growth and Channel Manager on pre-close deployment scoping for fleet and federal opportunities (technical sizing, implementation schedule, customer readiness, professional services attach).

  • Coordinate with Engineering and Operations on deployment-driven product and process feedback loops.

  • Partner with the Customer Success team on deployment-to-adoption handoff and post-go-live customer health.

  • Provide deployment health reporting to Executive Leadership; flag at-risk deployments and lead corrective action.

Required Experience

  • 8+ years of customer-facing delivery, professional services, or deployment leadership experience, including 3+ years leading deployment teams or programs.

  • Demonstrated track record delivering complex communications, networking, or public-safety technology deployments at scale (multi-site, multi-agency, mission-critical).

  • Strong working knowledge of LMR, LTE/5G, IP-based communications, interoperability, or related public-safety / first-responder communications technology.

  • Experience operating in SLED, federal civilian, or DoD delivery environments with the contracting and security posture those environments require.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate technical complexity into operational outcomes that first-responder customers can run on.

  • Comfort with 60–75% travel to customer sites, including occasional same-week travel in response to deployment escalations.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; capable of speaking credibly with both agency Chiefs and IT teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience with Mutualink, Motorola Solutions, L3Harris, Tait, JPS, or similar public-safety communications platforms.

  • Experience with federal Go-Kit / tactical communications deployments and FedRAMP / FISMA / CJIS-aligned delivery practices.

  • PMP, PgMP, or other formal delivery / program management certification.

  • Background in standing up a deployment function inside a growth-stage company.

Travel Expectations

This position is expected to include 60–75% travel in support of customer deployments, agency engagements, federal opportunities, on-site escalation response, partner engagements, and Mutualink-led customer events.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Mutualink, Inc. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The Dental Coding Specialist is responsible for accurately reviewing, assigning, and validating dental procedure codes (CDT codes) for patient services to ensure proper billing, insurance claim submission, and regulatory compliance. This role works closely with dental providers, billing teams, and insurance companies to maximize reimbursement and maintain accurate patient records.

  • Audit and submit insurance dental claims.
  • Resolve claim denials, coding discrepancies, and reimbursement issues.
  • Ensure compliance with dental coding guidelines, payer rules and regulations.
  • Maintain accurate patient billing and coding records.
  • Communicate with providers, staff, and insurance carriers regarding coding questions.
  • Stay current on coding updates, regulations, and industry best practices.

This role description is a general description of the essential job functions. It is not intended to describe all the duties the POSITION may perform.

  • Communication Skills

Effectively and respectably communicate with other individuals, whether it be a colleague, patient, or patient’s family member and appropriately enumerate information in a manner easily understood by all parties. We do this to foster a culture of understanding between all parties, especially in complex and difficult situations, to ultimately provide the best care possible to our patients and their families.

Ability to make the most appropriate decision in a given situation and then taking the next steps to ensure appropriate and timely completion. This requires conflict resolution skills, critical thinking skills, confidence in your ability to make the right decision in most situations. This also includes keeping up with your licensure and yearly training requirements within your area expertise along with MAHEC’s organizational training. Finally, the ability to apply the depth of knowledge maintained and gained through this process in real life scenarios as appropriate.

Showing the ability to meet difficult situations with grace, professionalism, and understanding. Within your area of expertise, showing respect and showing empathy where appropriate with your colleagues, patients, and their family at all times, even when its most difficult to do so. This is done, in part, by effective listening, being your authentic self, showing responsibility and dependability, and being patient with others.

Adherence to MAHEC’s founding principles and incorporating them every day. Having an analytical mind and ability to work autonomously to solve complex problems that may arise. The wherewithal to think logically through a difficult problem and come to an appropriate resolution for a given issue. Measures success by understanding where we are currently and where we want to go and then applying those new ideas to affect positive change.

title: Geotechnical Engineer - Underground
description:
• Work on complex underground geotechnical challenges at one of the world's largest integrated copper operations, where your recommendations directly influence mine safety, production performance, and long-term mine design.

  • Develop your technical expertise alongside experienced geotechnical professionals while gaining exposure to advanced monitoring technologies, seismic risk management, ground support design, and large-scale underground mining methods.

  • Enjoy a stable lifestyle with a home-every-night schedule, competitive compensation and benefits, and the opportunity to build a long-term career in a high-performing team committed to safety, inclusion, innovation, and continuous improvement.

At Rio Tinto, we are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and able to succeed. We actively encourage applications from women and from people with diverse backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We know that great technical capability comes in many forms, and we’re focused on building teams that reflect the communities we operate in and support each other to do their best work.

We’re Finding Better Ways™ to provide the materials the world needs, now and in the future. Our values – care, courage and curiosity – guide how we work and how we treat each other.

About the role

We are looking for an Underground Geotechnical Engineer to join the Kennecott Underground team and play a key role in supporting the safe, efficient, and sustainable operation of one of North America's premier underground copper mines.

This is an exciting opportunity for an engineer who is passionate about rock mechanics, underground mining, and geotechnical risk management. Working within a highly skilled technical team, you will gain exposure to a broad range of geotechnical challenges including ground support design, excavation stability, seismic risk management, instrumentation and monitoring programs, and stope performance assessments. Your work will directly influence operational decision-making and contribute to maintaining safe production across the underground mine.

This role offers excellent opportunities to expand your technical capability, build relationships across the business, and develop your career within a global mining organization focused on innovation, safety, and operational excellence.

Reporting to the Senior Geotechnical Engineer and working collaboratively with operational and functional teams, you will be responsible for:

  • Completing routine geotechnical tasks including development and production inspections, damage mapping, geotechnical data collection, analysis, and excavation stability assessments.

  • Conducting stope stability assessments and preparing geotechnical stope notes to support safe production.

  • Designing, implementing, and managing geotechnical instrumentation and monitoring programs to assess underground excavation performance and stability.

  • Developing, maintaining, and improving geotechnical databases to support analysis, design, risk management, and reporting.

  • Reviewing ground support, intersection, and stope support designs.

  • Conducting seismic hazard assessments and back analyses while supporting the identification, evaluation, and management of seismic risk.

  • Communicating geotechnical risks and recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

  • Collaborating with operations, mine planning, geology, and other teams to ensure geotechnical risks are effectively identified and managed.

About you

  • A commitment to the safety of yourself and your team.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Geotechnical Engineering, Geological Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geology, Mining Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • Demonstrated underground hard rock geotechnical engineering experience.

  • Strong understanding of underground mining methods and geotechnical hazard management.

  • Experience completing geotechnical inspections, data collection, stability assessments, and technical analysis.

  • Strong interpersonal, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • Familiarity with software including Rocscience (RocData, Dips, Unwedge), Leapfrog, IMS, mXrap, and Deswik.

  • A valid U.S. driver’s license and the ability to operate vehicles in both underground and open-pit mine settings.

What we offer

  • A work environment where safety is always the number one priority.

  • Competitive base salary reflective of your skills and experience with an annual incentive bonus.

  • Access to top-tier family-friendly health programs including medical, prescription drug, dental, vision, life insurance coverage, and various voluntary benefits.

  • Excellent retirement plan including up to 6% defined company contribution; Generous 401k matching program.

  • Attractive share ownership plan.

  • Comprehensive leave policies which cover all the moments that matter in life: PTO (paid time off), paid holidays, and paid bereavement leave.

  • A generous parental leave policy, which ensures you’re able to spend quality time with your new family.

  • Discount programs for leisure purposes and access to Virgin Pulse with incentives supporting your wellbeing.

  • Access to our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), which provides confidential counselling or expert guidance for you and your family to help get through life’s challenges.

Where you'll be working

Our Kennecott mine is a world-class, fully integrated copper mining operation, including a concentrator, smelter, and refinery, located just outside Salt Lake City, Utah, in the United States. We produce copper, precious metals including gold and silver, molybdenum, and sulfuric acid. Kennecott has been mining and processing minerals from the rich ore body of the Bingham Canyon Mine since 1903 and is one of the top producing mines in the world, comprising approximately 11 percent of U.S. annual copper production.


About Rio Tinto

Rio Tinto is a leading global mining and materials company. We operate in 35 countries where we produce iron ore, copper, aluminium, critical minerals, and other materials needed for the global energy transition and for people, communities, and nations to thrive.

We have been mining for 150 years and operate with knowledge built up across generations and continents. Our purpose is finding better ways to provide the materials the world needs – striving for innovation and continuous improvement to produce materials with low emissions and to the right environmental, social and governance standards. But we can’t do it on our own, so we’re focused on creating partnerships to solve problems, create win-win situations and meet opportunities.

Respect and Inclusion

Rio Tinto is committed to equal employment opportunity. All qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, sex, age, religion, national origin, disability, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

We are committed to an inclusive environment where people feel safe, respected and valued. We want our people to feel that all voices are heard and that a variety of perspectives are not only welcome but are essential to our success. We treat all our people fairly and with dignity.

Rio Tinto participates in E- Verify to confirm work authorization. Please visit http://www.ucis.gov/ for more information.

title: GTM System Engineer
description:
Own the data engine behind a fast-growing cybersecurity company's outbound motion.

Cytix is rebranding and rebuilding how we go to market. Cold outbound, partner outreach, intent-driven sales, hundreds of accounts in motion at any one time, and a sales floor that depends on someone keeping the data engine clean, fast, and intelligent. That someone is you.

You won't be starting from scratch. You'll inherit a working system: our Campaign Manager has spent over a year building the Clay-based pipeline that enriches contacts, scores leads, routes them to the right rep, and logs every activity in Salesforce. You take that, learn it inside out, and then make it better.

What you'll do

  • Own the data feeding our three outreach lanes: ABM (priority accounts with a multi-tier contact strategy), Intent (signals like hiring, buying intent, competitor activity and regulated-industry triggers), and Partner Outreach.

  • Hold the keys to the Clay pipeline. Enrichment, scoring, routing, automation logic.

  • Plug intent platforms into our sequencing workflow so signals turn into real conversations in real time.

  • Guard data hygiene like it's the family silver: deliverability, deduplication, opt-outs, sender reputation.

  • Tell the truth in numbers. Build the dashboards that let sales leadership see whether outbound is actually working.

  • Sit shoulder-to-shoulder with the SDR team every day. They depend on what you ship.

What you'll bring

Required:

  • A finished degree (any subject; STEM helpful but not required).

  • Comfort with data. You've used SQL, Python, or serious Excel formulas, even if not professionally.

  • Sharp, curious, and willing to dive into systems you don't understand yet.

  • Strong written and verbal communication. You'll work daily with sales reps; you have to explain technical decisions without being precious about them.

  • The temperament to be embedded with a sales team: ship fast, take direct feedback, fix things, ship again.

Strongly helps:

  • Exposure to SaaS, sales, or RevOps concepts. Anything that means 'pipeline' and 'MQL' aren't new words.

  • Hands-on experience with systems where data flows between them: CRMs, enrichment tools, spreadsheets, APIs.

  • Anything that proves you can ship: an automation project, a published analysis, a portfolio dashboard, a personal automation that does something useful.

What you'll get

  • Share options. If Cytix wins, you should too.

  • Enhanced maternity pay.

  • Octopus car scheme. Drive electric through salary sacrifice.

  • Dog-friendly office. Bring them along.

  • Inclusivity as standard. A team where you can do your best work as yourself, no asterisks.

About Cytix

Software never stops changing. Teams ship new code every day, through tickets, pull requests, releases, and increasingly with AI in the mix, but the way security keeps up with all that change hasn't really moved on. That's the problem we're solving. Cytix helps organisations understand which software changes actually matter, what should happen next, and how to prove the right call was made. Security understood, in other words.

We're a small team with big plans, so every person we hire genuinely shapes what Cytix becomes. That's why we're upfront about our five values: we interview for all of them, and they matter to us more than a perfect CV. They're things you do, not things you are, so have a read and see if they sound like you.

Make the first move. When the goal is clear but the path isn't, you get moving rather than waiting for perfect instructions. If you're blocked, you make a sensible call, say what you're assuming, and explain how you'd course-correct. We'd rather you act and be slightly wrong than sit still.

Find the smarter path. You ask why before how. You dig into what the real problem is instead of just building what the spec says, and you're happy to question 'that's how it's always been done' when the reason behind it has gone stale.

See it through. When something's yours, it lands. No loose ends, no surprises for whoever picks it up next. You keep people posted when things change, and if something falls between roles, you catch it.

Raise the bar. You do the best job possible in the time you've got, whether that's a day or a month. Sometimes that means deep craft; sometimes the smartest move is quick and scrappy. It's about good judgement, and we hold each other to it without blame or politics.

Play to win. You care about the mission but don't take yourself too seriously. You say 'I' when things go wrong and 'we' when they go right, trust teammates to do things their own way, and bring a bit of humour when the pressure's on.

Sound like you on a normal working day? We'd love to meet you.

title: Software Engineer
description:
Our Capability Development team develops bespoke software for our clients in the Cyber Security domain. We may be building assured software that prioritises engineering rigour and reliability, rapid solutions that bring together existing tooling for high-impact results, or blended operational systems that address real-world challenges in the field. Common to all is a commitment to technically led decisions, meaningful technical challenge, and engaging career paths where your work makes it off the shelf and into the hands of our customers.

Across our projects, we work with a range of platforms, languages and delivery environments. This may include web applications, native applications, automation, data processing, integration work, mobile platforms, Linux systems, cloud or on-premise deployments, and specialist operational environments. We are interested in engineers who are comfortable adapting to different technical contexts and choosing appropriate tools for the problem at hand.

This role is aimed at software engineers with experience delivering software projects using interpreted languages and modern development practices. You may have worked with languages such as Python, Rust, JavaScript, C++, TypeScript, Go or similar, alongside experience building user-facing systems, APIs, services, native applications or tooling. We are less concerned with a fixed technology stack and more interested in strong engineering fundamentals, practical problem solving, and the ability to deliver useful, maintainable software.

We are led by engineers and empowered to optimise our lightweight development processes with the knowledge gained from each project. We value people who take ownership, communicate clearly, work well in small teams, and enjoy seeing software make a difference.

We are ideally looking for a candidate who holds an active Security Clearance to join our team, however, we will consider sponsoring new clearances for candidates that meet our technical requirements.
Key Responsibilities
As part of our team, you may be:

  • Designing and developing new software products, tools or capabilities from early concept through to delivery.

  • Adding new features to, improving, or replacing components within existing systems.

  • Building prototypes to explore technical options, validate ideas and help shape project direction.

  • Developing web, native, service-side or automation-focused software depending on project need.

  • Integrating applications, APIs, third-party tools or internal systems to deliver practical outcomes.

  • Working with colleagues and customers to understand requirements and turn them into reliable software.


For this role, you will be hands-on in the day-to-day delivery of projects. Typically, this will see you working with one or two other colleagues at a time, taking responsibility for implementation decisions while contributing to wider project planning and delivery.

You will help maintain high engineering standards through clear design, readable code, testing, review and pragmatic technical decision-making. You may also support junior colleagues by sharing knowledge, encouraging good development practices, and helping the team balance quality, maintainability and realistic delivery timescales.
Desirable Skills
Successful candidates will have experience in some of the following areas:

  • Professional experience delivering software projects using interpreted or high-level languages.

  • Experience building web applications, APIs, services, automation, native applications or internal tools.

  • Comfortable working across different parts of a system, from user interfaces through to backend services, integration points and deployment environments.

  • Ability to understand requirements, make sensible technical decisions and deliver maintainable software.

  • Experience working with existing codebases, including debugging, refactoring and adding new functionality.

  • Familiarity with modern software engineering practices such as code review, automated testing, continuous integration and version control.

  • Comfortable learning unfamiliar technologies, libraries or platforms when required by a project.

  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work effectively in small, technically focused teams.

  • Clear communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions and collaborate with colleagues or customers.


This vacancy is for experienced software engineers who enjoy delivering practical, maintainable software across a range of technologies and project types. It is well suited to engineers who are adaptable, delivery-focused, and comfortable working across both web and native development environments.
Work Benefits

  • Promotions are based on technical excellence and reviewed regularly.

  • 25 days holiday per year (with bank holidays on top), option to buy up to 5 days per year.

  • Level up with an extra day of holiday per year, up to an extra 5 days, starting from 2 years' service.

  • We offer financial support to cover HMRC allowable costs of relocating if you’re moving to the area.

  • Training and development opportunities to support your career aspirations

  • O'Reilly books subscription which provides access to huge range of technical books

  • Regular events including internal technical conferences, company socials and pizza-fuelled lunchtime seminars.

  • Free seasonal fruit, tea, coffee, milk, squash and hot chocolate.


Health Benefits - Private medical including access to

  • Private online GP, and a helpline to speak with various healthcare professionals.

  • Physiotherapists, osteopaths or chiropractors for muscle, bone, and joint pain.

  • Mental health - counselling, and specialist consultations and treatment with psychologists and cognitive behavioural therapists.

  • Annual Health assessment.

Santiam Junction Maintenance Crew / District 3
Santiam Junction

The role:

Do you want to use your skills to make a difference? Join our hardworking Santiam Junction maintenance crew in this seasonal role to help keep Oregon’s roads and travelers safe! As part of our team, you will operate equipment necessary to maintain and repair roadways, highways, bridges and structures. You will also help with emergency cleanup and traffic control after storms, spills, incidents and more! Apply today!

This is a seasonal position that is expected to last approximately 6 months from date of hire. Seasonal positions are regular status, benefits eligible positions, which occur, terminate and recur periodically or regularly.

We provide a safe and reliable multimodal transportation system that connects people and helps Oregon's communities and economy thrive. We encourage people from all backgrounds and abilities to apply for our positions.

Before applying, visit our applicant information website to learn more about our process. If you are a current State of Oregon employee, you must apply through your employee Workday profile.

A day in the life:

  • Operate a variety of heavy and light equipment and tools to maintain and repair various surfaces.

  • Assist with weather related emergencies and operate snowplows, deicer trucks and other equipment to clear snow from roadways.

  • Clear debris, clear brush, mow grass and spray roadside vegetation.

  • Maintain and repair fences, guardrails, concrete barriers and milepost markers.

  • Maintain drainage systems, dig and clean ditches and repair culverts, inlets and erosion.

  • Maintain wooded areas which includes replanting, pruning, thinning or trimming trees, shrubs and groundcover.

  • Service and repair tools and motorized equipment.

  • Perform minor maintenance including janitorial work, landscaping, painting and light carpentry.

  • Exposure to noise, extreme heights, all weather conditions, heavy equipment, pesticides and hazardous waste materials is expected.

Minimum qualifications:

One year of experience performing basic highway maintenance work;

OR

Two years of general landscaping, maintenance, mechanical, farming, logging, and/or construction experience or training.

    • Sheltered RV pad space is available.

  • You must possess a current, valid commercial driver's license A (CDL-A) with a tanker endorsement, no air brake restrictions, no 5th wheel restrictions and no manual transmission restrictions, OR have the ability to acquire a class A commercial learner permit within 60 days of hire and a CDL-A with a tanker endorsement and restrictions removed within six months of hire (ODOT will cover training costs) to be considered eligible for this position.

Knowledge of provider reimbursement methodologies, provider network operations, compliance requirements, and healthcare data management required. Experience developing and executing strategy within a matrixed organization preferred.

At Goldman Sachs, our Engineers don't just make things - we make things possible. Change the world by connecting people and capital with ideas. The firm is seeking a dynamic, entrepreneurial developer to join the Commodities Technology team and play a key role in leading a range of development projects. The Commodities business is extremely focused on digitization, so this role will provide many challenging and rewarding opportunities for the successful candidate. The candidate will partner with engineers, traders, and salespeople to work on brand new projects focused on automation of sales and trading quoting, trade booking workflows, and data platform to systematically process data and share actionable insights to enable trading decisions. The candidate will directly experience their impact as they see the automation of the Commodities trading franchise through their work.
